stories.title: Dubai-based Akib denies links to terror plot:Akib says he won’t betray the country, urges authorities not to label him as terrorist
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested four suspected terrorists accused of plotting attacks across several cities, including Lucknow. Investigators revealed that the group had received an offer from Pakistan-based handlers, greater the scale of terror, higher the financial reward. However, one key suspect, Akib Khan, who allegedly connected the group with Pakistani handler Abu Bakar, remains absconding. Akib Khan issues statement from Dubai Akib, a resident of Meerut, is currently in Dubai, from where he has been posting videos on social media denying all allegations. In his statements, he insists that he has no involvement in terrorism and claims he is being falsely implicated. In one video, he said, 'This is our country. We will not betray it, nor will we sell our integrity. Do not label us terrorists, catch those who are guilty.' He further stated that no evidence exists linking him to funding or recruiting individuals. Refuting claims that he facilitated communication between suspects and handlers, he challenged authorities to produce call records as proof. Read the report 'We will not sell our faith' In his videos, Akib emphasised his loyalty to India, stating he would never compromise his faith or country for money. He claimed he has been living in Dubai since 2019, working as a driver and earning a legitimate livelihood. 'I earn my living honestly. I belong to a respectable family. Do not brand me a terrorist,' he said, adding that he is willing to answer any questions if approached directly. Multiple videos shared online Over the past five days, Akib has posted three videos across multiple Instagram accounts, where he has over 40,000 followers. In each, he has maintained his innocence and rejected allegations of involvement in any terror-related activities. In one video, he asserted, 'I love my country deeply. I am a Pathan, I would rather lose my life than bow down. The accusations against me are completely false.' Appeal to PM and CM Akib also appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, urging them to ensure a fair investigation. He claimed he had previously cooperated with police and shared accurate information. 'I have nothing to do with this. I drive a car and support my family through hard work. Please catch the real culprits,' he said. Conspiracy to target multiple cities According to ATS investigations, the four arrested suspects, Saqib alias Devil, Vikas Gehlawat alias Raunak, Lokesh alias Babu alias Papla Pandit, and Arbab—were part of a wider conspiracy to carry out blasts in multiple cities following an initial attack in Lucknow. From their possession, authorities recovered a chemical-filled container, seven mobile phones, 24 pamphlets, and Aadhaar cards. During interrogation, Saqib was identified as the mastermind. He reportedly confessed that Akib had introduced him to Pakistani handler Abu Bakar. Instructions from Pakistani handlers ATS officials stated that handlers based in Pakistan provided detailed operational guidance through audio recordings and social media platforms. These included reconnaissance methods, target selection, and execution strategies. The suspects were instructed to leave the state immediately after carrying out attacks. They were also told to record videos of the aftermath and send them back to handlers. Several such audio clips have been recovered from their mobile phones. How did ATS uncover the network ? The investigation began with an arson incident in Bijnor on 4 March 2026, when a pickup van belonging to Nimish Rastogi was set on fire. Police arrested Abuzar and Zaid on 12 March in connection with the case. During questioning, it emerged that Abuzar was facing financial difficulties and had sought help from his cousin, Mohammad Zaid. Zaid connected him with Abu Bakar through Telegram. Under instructions, Abuzar targeted vehicles belonging to the Hindu community and set fire to a van near a temple. He recorded the act and sent the video to the handler, after which money was transferred to his account. Further investigation revealed that Zaid was part of 12 Telegram groups linked to such activities. Both the ATS and the National Investigation Agency (NIA) are now probing the case. Surveillance and links to Akib As the investigation progressed, links between Saqib and Abu Bakar were uncovered. ATS then placed Saqib’s mobile number under surveillance, leading to the unravelling of the broader network. Akib’s alleged role as an intermediary connecting local operatives to foreign handlers has become a key focus of the probe. Action against police officials The case has also led to disciplinary action against two police officials. A complaint had been filed on 23 November 2025 at Najibabad police station against Maizul, Akib, and an unidentified individual. The then Station House Officer, Satyendra Singh Malik, contacted Maizul and arranged a video call with Akib. During the call, Akib dismissed concerns, claiming that what appeared to be an AK-47 was merely a toy and that a suspected grenade was actually a perfume bottle. Accepting this explanation, the police filed a final report, effectively giving them a clean chit. However, following recent developments, the SSP suspended SHO Malik and attached Circle Officer Nitesh Pratap Singh to the police lines on 5 April. With multiple agencies involved and fresh leads emerging, the case continues to unfold. Authorities are focusing on tracing financial transactions, digital communications, and international links to dismantle the network completely.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav shown as 'Rehman Dakait' in hoardings:Youth Against Mafia's posters asks, 'Lyari Raj or Dhurandhar CM, what do you want?'
stories.summary: The film ‘Dhurandhar 2’ has triggered a political storm in Uttar Pradesh. Controversy has erupted over the portrayal of a character resembling mafia don Atiq Ahmed, shown as having links with Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI and a terrorist organisation. Opposition parties, including the Samajwadi Party (SP), have termed it BJP propaganda. Meanwhile, hoardings targeting SP chief Akhilesh Yadav have appeared across Lucknow. Hoardings target Akhilesh Yadav In hoardings installed at several locations, Akhilesh has been depicted as ‘Rehman Dakait’, the villain from the film Dhurandhar. The caption reads, ‘Akhilesh’s Lyari Raj’. On one side of the hoarding is an image of Yogi Adityanath performing Kanya Pujan, labelled ‘Dhurandhar CM’. The hoarding poses the question, ‘What do you want?’ ‘Youth Against Mafia’ campaign The hoardings, put up by an organisation named ‘Youth Against Mafia’, feature news clippings beneath Akhilesh’s image highlighting riots during his tenure in Muzaffarnagar, Meerut and Shamli. On the opposite side, under CM Yogi’s image, are clippings of action taken against mafias such as Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari. Installed across key locations in Lucknow These hoardings have been installed at major intersections across Lucknow, including areas around the Chief Minister’s residence. Their appearance has intensified political debate and drawn attention from passers-by and local residents. The hoardings also display the names and photographs of office bearers of ‘Youth Against Mafia’, including Executive President Ashutosh Singh and General Secretary Abhinav Tiwari. The riots during the SP government have been labelled as ‘Lyari Raj’. SP tenure labelled ‘Lyari Raj’ Through these displays, a direct attack has been made on the SP by referencing riots in Muzaffarnagar, Meerut and Shamli. By terming these incidents ‘Lyari Raj’, the hoardings attempt to suggest weak law and order during that period. CM Yogi projected as ‘Dhurandar’ In contrast, the hoardings highlight actions against organised crime, projecting Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as ‘Dhurandar’. Newspaper clippings related to cases involving Atiq Ahmed, Mukhtar Ansari and Mukim Kala have been included to underline a message of strict law enforcement.

stories.title: Drivers will not feel drowsy on Ganga Expressway:Rest facilities available at every 75 km; Meerut to Prayagraj journey cut to 6 hours
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh’s 594 km-long Ganga Expressway is nearing completion, with finishing work currently underway. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to inaugurate it soon. Once operational, the expressway will connect western UP to eastern regions, reducing travel time between Meerut and Prayagraj to just six hours, compared to the current 11–12 hours. The expressway is equipped with several advanced public convenience facilities, including rest areas, trauma centres for medical emergencies, and food courts. Rumble strips have been installed along the road, raised markings that create vibrations when tyres pass over them, alerting drivers and reducing the risk of accidents caused by fatigue. Fuel stations are already operational, toll plaza staff have been deployed, signage has been installed, and speed monitoring systems are active. Before its public opening, a ground report journey from Meerut to Prayagraj was conducted to assess readiness. Route and entry restrictions Named after the Ganga River, the expressway passes through 12 districts located along its basin. It begins near Bijauli village, about 7 km from Meerut, at the Hapur border. National Highway-334, connecting Meerut to Haridwar, Saharanpur, and Bulandshahr, also passes nearby. Entry and exit points were found closed during the visit due to security concerns, as bikers had begun entering the expressway for stunts. Officials clarified that only cars and heavy vehicles will be permitted, with motorcycles prohibited. High-speed corridor and toll system After obtaining permission from UPEDA, the journey began, with vehicles quickly reaching speeds of 110 km/h on the largely empty stretch. The first toll plaza was encountered in Meerut. Officials stated that there will be two main toll plazas, one in Meerut and another in Prayagraj. Additionally, 15 ramp toll plazas have been constructed at entry and exit points across districts, allowing access after toll payment. Proposed toll rates have already been determined. Rumble strips to prevent fatigue About 20 km into the journey, noticeable vibrations were felt in the vehicle. These were caused by rumble strips placed along the road edges. Such strips are designed to counter driver fatigue caused by long, uninterrupted high-speed driving. The vibration alerts drivers who may be drowsy, helping prevent accidents. These strips extend across the entire stretch from Meerut to Prayagraj. PPP model and fuel infrastructure The expressway has been developed under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model and divided into four sections. The Meerut to Badaun stretch was constructed by Ideal Road Builders Infrastructure, while the remaining three sections, from Badaun to Hardoi, Hardoi to Unnao, and Unnao to Prayagraj, were developed by Adani Enterprises, accounting for 75% of the project. A total of nine public convenience centres have been built along the route. These include petrol pumps, food plazas, cafeterias, dormitories, hotel facilities, and trauma centres. Fuel stations are available every 75 km, making this the first expressway in UP where fuel infrastructure is operational even before public opening. All petrol pumps are operated directly by Bharat Petroleum under the company-owned, company-operated (COCO) model. Flexible stay and emergency healthcare Food plazas offer affordable options, while dormitories and hotel rooms are available for drivers and passengers. Unlike traditional hotels, payments are calculated on an hourly basis rather than a fixed 24-hour charge. Primary health centres have been established near toll plazas. According to staff, emergency response time is targeted at 20 minutes. Ambulances are equipped with oxygen cylinders, first-aid medicines, and life-saving equipment. Serious cases will be transferred to trauma centres. Engineering challenges: Ramganga Bridge In Badaun, the expressway features a 720-metre-long bridge over the Ramganga river. Construction posed significant challenges due to riverbank erosion. Initially, the river flowed 200 metres away from the bridge site but later changed course, damaging nearby areas. Engineers eventually diverted the flow and completed the structure at a cost of ₹122 crore. Airstrip for defence operations At Jalalabad in Shahjahanpur, a 3.5 km airstrip has been developed along the expressway. The stretch has removable dividers, allowing it to function as a runway during wartime. Fighter jets can land here even at night. See day and night pictures of the plane landing - On 2 May 2025, the Indian Air Force conducted landing and take-off exercises involving 16 aircraft, including Rafale, Sukhoi, Mirage-2000, MiG-29, Jaguar, and transport aircraft such as Hercules, AN-32, and Mi-17-V5. This airstrip enhances operational readiness, serves as an alternative runway if airbases are compromised, and aids disaster management by enabling rapid deployment of relief materials and personnel. Connectivity and endpoint Travelling through Shahjahanpur, Hardoi, Unnao, and Rae Bareli, the route connects with improved highways, including the Lucknow–Prayagraj four-lane corridor. The expressway ends near Judapur Dandu, about 15 km before Prayagraj, where National Highway-19 (Delhi–Kolkata route) passes underneath. From this junction, Prayagraj can be accessed directly, while Varanasi is reachable within two hours via NH-19. Ayodhya, located about 160 km away, is also well connected, boosting religious tourism. Cost, expansion and economic impact The foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 18 December 2021 in Shahjahanpur. The project cost is approximately ₹37,350 crore, with an average cost of ₹62.87 crore per kilometre. Around ₹9,500 crore was spent on land acquisition, with farmers receiving compensation up to four times the circle rate. Land prices near Bijauli have already surged, and an industrial corridor is planned in the area. The expressway reduces the Meerut–Prayagraj distance from 684 km (via Kanpur) to 594 km. It also eliminates the need to travel via Lucknow to access the Agra Expressway for Delhi-bound journeys. Plans are underway to extend it to Haridwar. The corridor will improve connectivity across districts, including Pratapgarh, Rae Bareli, Unnao, Shahjahanpur, Hardoi, Badaun, Amroha, Sambhal, Bulandshahr, and Hapur. Key benefits across sectors Real Estate: Improved connectivity is expected to drive up land prices, particularly in residential sectors. Religious Tourism: Easier access to Prayagraj, Varanasi, Garhmukteshwar, Haridwar, and Ayodhya will boost pilgrim movement. Industry: Better transport links will facilitate the movement of raw materials and encourage industrial growth in smaller towns.

stories.title: Kanpur racket trapped youths via gaming apps:Doctors cited US-UK research claims longer life with one kidney
stories.summary: A disturbing kidney transplant racket in Kanpur has come to light, where young men were trapped through gaming apps and coerced into donating their kidneys. Victims, after losing money on these platforms, were pressured into organ donation with promises of ₹20–25 lakh in return. If they resisted, they were sent research papers from universities in the United States and London, highlighting cases of people living healthy lives with a single kidney. Gradually brainwashed, many victims agreed to undergo surgery. Ayush Kumar, one such victim, had his kidney removed following the same pattern. A mule bank account in his name was opened at a Delhi bank, and police are now tracing financial transactions. Statements of jailed agent Shivam Agarwal are set to be recorded. Over 50 transplants raise alarm Investigations have revealed that more than 50 kidney transplants were conducted in Kanpur alone. Police have arrested nine individuals, including doctors and operating theatre technicians, while six more suspects have been identified and are being pursued. The scale of the operation raised critical questions about how donors were sourced. During questioning, Ayush’s mobile phone records exposed key details of the network and its methods. Telegram gaming trap operated by doctors Police investigations indicate that two doctors, Dr Afzal and Dr Mudassir Ali, created groups on the Telegram messaging app. These groups circulated links to task-based gaming platforms. Players were required to create accounts and were initially encouraged with bonus funds and easy wins. At the outset, participants were allowed to earn small amounts, which were credited to their accounts. However, as they progressed, the tasks became increasingly difficult, requiring higher financial investments. Gradually, players began losing money. At regular intervals, messages appeared urging them to borrow funds to continue playing. Many took loans in the hope of recovering losses, only to fall deeper into debt. From Debt to Coercion: ‘Sell your kidney’ Once individuals were financially distressed, gang members contacted them, demanding repayment. During these conversations, victims were persuaded to consider kidney donation as a solution. They were told that the human body has two kidneys and that one could be donated without affecting quality of life. The gang promised payments of ₹20–25 lakh, suggesting victims could repay debts and lead comfortable lives. According to DCP West SM Qasim Abidi, psychological pressure played a key role. Victims were sent curated studies claiming people born with one kidney lived normal lives. This systematic conditioning eventually led to consent for surgery. In Ayush Kumar’s case from Begusarai, Bihar, he was convinced to donate his kidney for ₹9.5 lakh. Ayush’s messages reveal distress WhatsApp messages sent by Ayush to Dr Afzal reveal the emotional toll. He expressed regret over wasted time, inability to focus on exams, and mounting distress. He requested to withdraw from the process and repay ₹6,000 gradually over two to three months. He also mentioned delays in the surgery and refused a longer waiting period of 30–40 days, stating that timely completion mattered more than higher payment. Role of key agent Parvez Saifi Police are bringing Parvez Saifi from Meerut to Kanpur. He allegedly facilitated the movement of doctors for transplant procedures. During Parul Tomar’s transplant, Parvez brought Dr Rohit’s team and stayed in Kanpur for 10 days. His involvement has been traced across several of the 50 known operations. Parvez has a criminal history, with cases of robbery in Meerut and Baghpat, dacoity in Ghaziabad, and attempted murder. During Parul’s transplant, her husband Vikas Tomar and brother Divyank Ahuja were present. However, Vikas left before a police raid, while Divyank remained. Vikas has not appeared before investigators since. After the procedure, ₹22 lakh was reportedly paid to Dr Afzal. Authorities believe a viral video showing bundles of cash may be linked to this transaction. From hospital guard to network operator A key figure, Ajay, emerged during the investigation. He had previously worked as a guard at Hallet Hospital under a compassionate appointment scheme. After one year, he opened Star Hospital in Keshavpuram, Kalyanpur, employing Dr Rohan and Dr Narendra. Later, these doctors, along with Sandeep from Kannauj, established Medilife Hospital in Maswanpur. Sandeep remains absconding. Ajay stated that most cases at his hospital were abortions and that financial losses in 2022–23 forced its closure. He admitted introducing the doctors to agent Shivam Kada, after which kidney transplants began at Medilife Hospital. However, Ajay denied knowledge of financial arrangements between the parties. After three hours of questioning, the police issued him a notice and released him. Authorities are also investigating the role of a South African woman named Arabica, whose video recently surfaced. Police believe agent Shivam Agarwal is a crucial link in identifying her. He was seen examining someone with a stethoscope in the footage. Officials have contacted the South African embassy to verify her identity, visa details, and travel history. Preliminary findings suggest she met gang members in Delhi, but further details remain unclear. Expanding investigation across states DCP Abidi described Shivam Agarwal as the central link in the network. Police have sought a seven-day remand to extract further information. He is expected to be taken to Meerut and Delhi for additional questioning. Another agent, Naveen Pandey from Prayagraj, has also been identified. When police visited his residence in Kanpur, his family claimed he worked at a battery company and was unaware of his alleged involvement. Investigators believe he managed hospital arrangements for illegal transplants in the Delhi-NCR region. Hospitals under scanner Police have identified nine hospitals across four cities, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Lucknow, and Kanpur, linked to the racket. Letters have been sent to Chief Medical Officers in these districts, and their roles are under investigation. Nationwide probe intensifies The cyber team has traced a key suspect to Maharashtra, prompting the deployment of a police team. Another team visited Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in Lucknow to question Ayush further. During the inquiry, it emerged that Ayush had initially provided false information about studying at Graphic Era University, Dehradun. He later admitted he is a student of Uttaranchal University. The investigation continues to unravel a complex network combining cyber fraud, psychological manipulation, and illegal organ trade.

stories.title: Shikshamitras to get ₹18,000 per month in UP:Madrasa teacher recruitment to be done via commission; 22 proposals approved in cabinet
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet on Tuesday approved 22 proposals. Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh announced an increase in honorarium for Shikshamitras and instructors. Shikshamitras will now receive ₹18,000 per month, while instructors will get ₹17,000. He stated that the revised pay has been effective from 1 April, with increased payments set to be credited from 1 May. Earlier, instructors received ₹9,000 and Shikshamitras ₹10,000 per month. The state currently has 1,42,229 Shikshamitras and 24,000 instructors. Madrasa recruitment and new guidelines The Cabinet also approved that recruitment of teachers in government-aided madrasas will now be conducted through the Education Service Selection Commission. This means candidates will be required to pass an examination, replacing the earlier system of recruitment at the madrasa level. New operational guidelines for madrasas will also be introduced. These include a mandatory eight-hour study schedule, similar to regular schools. Online attendance will be recorded for principals, teachers and students, and a comprehensive database of students will be maintained. 1. Beautification of statues of social reformers Minister Asim Arun announced that under the ‘Dr B.R. Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme’, statues of eminent personalities who contributed to social reform will be upgraded and beautified at public places. Works will include installation of canopies, boundary structures and overall beautification around statues of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar and other reformers. Around ₹10 lakh will be spent per statue, with ₹1 crore allocated per विधानसभा constituency. Detailed guidelines for the scheme will be released on 14 April. No new statues will be installed; instead, existing statues set up until 31 December 2025 will be upgraded. This includes statues of Sant Ravidas, Kabirdas, Jyotiba Phule and other prominent social reformers across communities. It was also stated that during the Samajwadi Party government, statues and memorials of such leaders had been disrespected. 2. Land rights for displaced families Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said that 12,000 families who migrated from Pakistan during Partition have been granted land ownership rights. This includes 4,000 families in Pilibhit, 2,350 in Lakhimpur Kheri, 3,856 in Bijnor and 2,170 in Rampur. Additionally, 99 displaced Hindu families will receive land in Kanpur on a lease of ₹1. 3. Approval for tablet procurement and investment proposals Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, said approval has been granted for a tender to procure 25 lakh tablets. So far, 60 lakh tablets have been distributed under the Swami Vivekananda Youth Empowerment Scheme. A total of eight proposals from the department have been cleared, including provisions for subsidies to investors. 4. 49 bus stands to be developed on PPP model Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh stated that three proposals from the Transport Department have been approved. The government will develop 49 bus stands under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. Earlier, approval had been granted for 23 such bus stands. The aim is to ensure at least one PPP-based bus stand in every district, with an estimated investment of ₹4,000 crore. Land transfer proposals have also been approved. Land in Ratanpur Husainpur village will be provided free of cost for a bus station in Sikandrarao, Hathras. Similarly, land from the Irrigation Department in Narora, Bulandshahr, will be used for a bus station and depot workshop, while Public Works Department land in Tulsipur tehsil of Balrampur will be used for a bus stand. 5. New university in Gorakhpur The Forest Minister announced that a Horticulture and Forestry University will be established in Gorakhpur. The project will cost ₹491.0777 crore and will be developed over 50 hectares in the Campierganj area. The university will offer BSc, MSc, PhD and diploma courses. stories.title: Elderly man stabbed to death in public:Victim attacked over 12 times in Bhadohi; rescuer also targeted
stories.summary: A youth stabbed an elderly man to death in broad daylight in Bhadohi. The elderly man was drinking tea in the market. Just then, the youth came and suddenly attacked him. When he ran to save himself, the accused chased him and started stabbing him with a knife. When people came to save the elderly man, the accused attacked them too with a knife. The youth stabbed the elderly man more than 12 times. He fell to the ground drenched in blood. After this, the accused fled from there. The accused came to his house about 1 kilometer away from the crime scene and locked the door from inside. Police reached his house and broke down the door to enter. During this, the accused showed a knife to the police. He was somehow arrested. The accused was angry about not getting water for irrigation. The incident is from Wednesday evening, around 5 pm, in the Chauri police station area. CCTV footage of this has also emerged. Police are interrogating him. Bachhan Ram (65), a resident of Chauri police station area, had been working as a pump operator at a government tubewell for 20 years. On Tuesday, the accused, Shravan Gautam, came to get a water supply for his fields. Bachhan Ram asked him to come the next day. This angered Shravan. On Wednesday, around 5 PM, Bachhan Ram went to the market to have tea. Meanwhile, Shravan also reached there and started abusing the elderly man. Before he could understand anything, the accused pulled out a knife and attacked him. When the elderly man ran to save himself, the accused chased him and started stabbing him with the knife. When people came from behind to save him, he attacked them too. When the elderly man fell on the ground covered in blood, the accused fled from there. Villagers accused the police of forcibly taking possession of the body. Attacked with knife while drinking tea Eyewitness to the incident, Irrigation Department's Jiledar Ashok Kumar Dubey said that we were sitting and drinking tea. Just then, the accused came and attacked Bacchan Ram repeatedly with a knife. After several blows, Bacchan Ram fell to the ground, seriously injured and soaked in blood. People were preparing to take him to the hospital. During this time, he kept asking for water continuously. Ashok's right thumb was injured in the intervention. The elderly man was stabbed about 12 times with a knife. Son says, 'They misled and took father's body' There was chaos at the time of the incident. Whoever came to save the elderly man, the youth started attacking them with a knife. The elderly man's son, Pramod, says that this incident happened only due to a water dispute. Pramod made serious allegations against the police and said that while taking my father in a private vehicle, the police misled us at the railway crossing and took the body into their custody. Accused's mother said that behavior changed since Navratri The mother of the accused, Shravan Kumar, said that their crop needed water, but she didn't know what the dispute was about. The knife used in the murder is not from the house. I have never seen that knife before. Shravan's mental state and health were normal. During Navratri, Shravan's behavior had changed significantly. He was neither talking to anyone nor eating or drinking anything. Shravan has a one-year-old daughter who has been at her maternal home with her mother for the past two months. Died while being taken for treatment CO Gyanpur Prabhat Rai said that a dispute occurred over an old rivalry. The elderly person died on the way while being taken for treatment. Another person sustained minor injuries in the incident. The accused has been taken into custody and is being interrogated. Several other aspects are also being investigated. The body has been taken into possession; further action is being taken.

stories.title: Burqa-clad woman robs jewellery shop at gunpoint in Ayodhya:Escapes with accomplice on bike after threatening shopkeeper
stories.summary: A woman in a burqa robbed a gold necklace and chain from a jewelry shop at gunpoint in Ayodhya. When the shopkeeper chased her, she showed the pistol and threatened to kill him. The woman fled with her accomplice, who was already waiting outside the shop with a bike. The shopkeepers chased the robber woman but could not catch her. The traders informed the police. The police have cordoned off the area and started searching for the suspects, but so far, no trace of the accused has been found. The police examined CCTV footage from the surrounding area, in which the accused can be seen fleeing. The incident is from the Rudauli police station area. Woman asked for gold necklace and chain Mahesh, a resident of Mohalla Kothi Bazaar in Rudauli Kotwali area, is a gold and silver trader. His shop, named Mahesh Jewellers, is located in Agrawal Complex, 900 meters away from his home. On Thursday afternoon, around 12:30 PM, a woman wearing a burqa arrived at the shop. She had a backpack with her. She told Mahesh, "I want to buy a necklace and a gold chain." Mahesh placed a gold necklace and a gold chain in front of her. After this, the woman asked Mahesh for water. Mahesh sent Ankit Kumar, who works in the shop, to bring water and samosas. After some time, Ankit Kumar came back with samosas and water. He gave the water and samosas to the woman. But the woman refused to eat the samosas. She took the water bottle. She says, 'I don't eat samosas, get me sweets' The accused woman told Mahesh that I don't eat samosas. Get me, sweets. Mahesh Kumar sent Ankit Kumar to get barfi. Ankit went to get barfi. Meanwhile, the shop employee Maniram picked up the necklace and chain and placed them on the counter. Just then, the woman stood up and started wandering around inside the shop. Mahesh asked her what the matter was. The woman said that my husband has gone to withdraw money. He hasn't come yet. I'm just looking for him. After this, she came and stood near the counter. Mahesh started putting other items in the cupboard, when the accused woman picked up the gold necklace and the chain kept in the box. Then she picked up her bag. Just then, when shopkeeper Mahesh stopped her, she pulled out a pistol from her waist. Pointing it at Mahesh, she said If you move forward, I'll shoot you. After this, she ran out of the shop. Mahesh and Maniram chased her while raising an alarm. Fled with jewelry while showing pistol The woman ran on foot from the shop and escaped with her accomplice, who was waiting with a bike at some distance. Mahesh informed that the necklace weighed 26 grams. As per the market rate on April 2, the price of 22-carat gold is approximately ₹3 lakh 60 thousand. The traders informed the police. Qila Chowki in-charge Jitendra Singh reached the spot. On the orders of the SSP, the market was cordoned off, and a check was done. But the accused woman could not be caught. Superintendent of Police Rural Balwant Chaudhary said, Two police teams are deployed. More than 50 CCTV cameras have been examined. The incident will be revealed soon.

stories.title: Akhilesh unhappy with SP MLAs over Sambhal SP reception visit:SP chief alleges BJP members linked to fake currency and kidney scams
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has expressed displeasure over three SP MLAs and a district president attending the reception of Sambhal SP KK Bishnoi, saying they should have avoided it. He added that the leaders will be spoken to and counselled. Addressing a press conference after a party meeting on Thursday, Akhilesh targeted the Bharatiya Janata Party government led by Yogi Adityanath on multiple issues. Referring to the recent kidney case in Kanpur, he alleged that the Health Minister is unaware of ground realities and is instead focused on criticizing opposition rallies. He further accused BJP members of being linked to fake currency and kidney scams, and said they are claiming credit for projects initiated during the SP government. In a sharp remark, Akhilesh said that while BJP leaders take credit, “one ‘plant’ has grown significantly under their rule,” alluding to repeated ganja seizures. He added that a film could be made on ‘Ganja Ganj’ and suggested another one on ‘Dhuan Dhar’. Read the major statements made by Akhilesh Yadav... 1- BJP leaders' language changed after Dadri rally Akhilesh Yadav said that after the Dadri rally, the language of BJP leaders has changed. They are trying to take credit for projects started during the SP government, such as River Front, Metro and JPNIC. BJP should clarify whether they are saying these things in reality or under influence. 2- As soon as elections end, the entire BJP battalion will gather in UP As soon as the elections conclude, the entire BJP army will come to UP. We are watching, where elections are happening, what the BJP and the Election Commission are doing together there. Akhilesh, giving the example of West Bengal, said that many officers were removed there. But, such action was not taken in Uttar Pradesh during the elections. Despite serious allegations against some officers, no action was taken against them. We, the people of the organization, will work together on the ground. 3- Those framing our workers will go to jail Our workers are being framed. Those who have framed our workers will be sent to jail. Regarding the Deoria fake currency case, he said that the matter there is different. Fake notes are coming into the country, and real ones are going out of the country. He asked if the picture tells everything, then whose side is the picture on? 4- Any BJP leader should hold a press conference under a water tank Akhilesh Yadav challenged BJP leaders, saying, "Tell the BJP people to stand under a water tank and hold a press conference. Come and walk on the Green Corridor, then you will understand how much corruption has taken place." Now know about the Sambhal SP's reception matter... Sambhal's SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi got married to IPS Anshika Verma on March 29 in Rajasthan. Their reception was held in Jodhpur on March 30. MLAs, MPs and other VVIPs from UP attended the wedding and reception. SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood from Sambhal, MLA Pinky Yadav from Asmoli, MLA Ramkhiladi Yadav from Gunnour and SP district president Asgar Ali Ansari also participated in it. Displeasure was expressed on the X handle named 'SP Media Cell' over SP members attending this reception. Meanwhile, after the tweet surfaced, all the MLAs and the district president deleted their posts congratulating the SP. However, when district president Asgar Ali was asked about this, he said he had no information about it. Read what SP Media Cell wrote on X handle Written on the Twitter handle named SP's Media Cell - At the wedding of a controversial and BJP-minded Superintendent of Police in Jodhpur, many socialists were invited, sensing the changing political atmosphere. All such BJP supporters and officials, who have committed atrocities on society at the behest of the BJP based on caste and religion. They will increase their rapport with socialists to avoid action by sensing the changing government and changing political winds. But, it is our responsibility as socialists to maintain a proper distance from such anti-social elements. Apart from politics and etiquette, we also have our own moral and social responsibilities, which we need to understand. We must maintain an appropriate distance from those anti-social elements, whether they are in the government, in administration or in any party. We have to expose them.

stories.title: FIR filed against Prayagraj neurosurgeon Dr. Kartikeya over ‘bad touch’:Student alleges clothes removed on pretext of treatment; forced despite refusal
stories.summary: An FIR has been registered against Dr Kartikeya Sharma, a well-known neurosurgeon in Prayagraj, over allegations of ‘bad touch’. A BA student has accused him of molestation. The student claims the doctor made her remove her clothes and then touched her with bad intent. Civil Lines police have registered a case based on her complaint, and she has been sent for a medical examination. The incident allegedly took place around 10:30 pm on Wednesday in the Clive Road area, where the 55-year-old doctor lives and runs his clinic from home. He is known to see patients late into the night. The 24-year-old student, a resident of Dhoomnaganj, had come with her brother for migraine treatment and was given token number 74. Her brother said he had to leave for urgent work and left his sister at the clinic. “When I returned, there was a commotion. My sister told me everything. I then informed our family and the police,” he said. A video of the incident has also surfaced, showing the doctor inside his house with the gate closed, arguing with the student’s family members outside. The student can be heard crying and asking, “Why did you make me remove my clothes?” The doctor has denied all allegations, saying he did nothing wrong. Police said the matter is under investigation. The student's number came at 10:30 PM The student's father has passed away. Her family consists of her mother and brother. Her brother works in a private job. The student told the police in her complaint that around 10:30 PM, my number came. When I reached the chamber, the doctor sent the other patients out, saying that an examination needed to be done. When I was left alone in the cabin, both doors of the chamber were locked from the inside. He started removing my clothes, and threatened me when I resisted The student said that after this, saying he would conduct an examination, the doctor started removing my upper clothes. He started molesting me. Then he asked me to remove my lower clothes as well. I got scared. I said I don't want to get examined, then he started forcing me. When I started crying, he threatened me and backed off. After this, he didn't open the doors until I had fixed my clothes. Called brother on phone, narrated her ordeal The student said that I came out and immediately called my brother. Seeing my condition, the patients and attendants already present surrounded the doctor. They started questioning him. When my brother came, I told him everything. Other family members also arrived. Dial 112 was informed. After some time, police from the Civil Lines station also arrived. Then the student was taken to the police station along with her family members. Patients entered the doctor's chamber, gave him a piece of their mind The student's family members said that when the daughter came out crying, other patients and attendants asked her the reason. When she narrated her ordeal, people entered the doctor's chamber. They started giving him a piece of their mind. At this, the doctor called his staff and got everyone thrown out. The gate was locked from the inside. Doctor said- I was examining the stomach In this entire matter, Dr. Kartikeya Sharma said- The girl had come. I examined her stomach. I won't deny this. Apart from this, whatever the girl has said is false. As for the female staff, they were on duty at that time. For a while, she had gone to give an injection to another patient. This took barely 3 minutes. If a female patient has to be checked, the doors have to be closed. The girl has been undergoing treatment for several years. She is a patient of psychosis, meaning depression. Earlier, she was admitted once to my hospital, Guru Gobind Singh Memorial Hospital. ACP Civil Lines Vidyut Goyal informed- Police reached the spot on the student's complaint. Investigation was conducted. The doctor was also questioned. For now, a case has been registered based on the statement. The matter is being thoroughly investigated. Who is Dr. Kartikeya?

stories.title: PWD uses 85% of allocated budget:Builds 3,235 bridges and develops 50 km of model roads across Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: The Public Works Department (PWD) of Uttar Pradesh was able to spend only 85% of its budget in the financial year 2025-26. The department had received a budget of 36 thousand 293 crore 95 lakh rupees for the financial year 2025-26. In comparison, the department spent 30 thousand 581 crore 98 lakh rupees. The department constructed a record 3,235 bridges in this financial year. Under the 'Setu Bandhan' scheme, 1,111 crore rupees were spent solely on the construction of 10 large bridges. This time, the department also built 50 km-long model roads. 5 Thousand crore more spent compared to last year The PWD department also surpassed the target of 28 thousand crore set by the government. It achieved over-achievement by spending 28,087 crore rupees. Whereas in the previous financial year 2024-25, the department had spent 23,850 crore rupees. The PWD department is under the Chief Minister. He continuously monitored the department's work. He increased the financial spending limit for officials. Due to the review of every scheme and continuous monitoring, the department achieved this target. The department, led by Principal Secretary Ajay Chauhan and Chief Engineer Ashok Kumar Dwivedi, continuously monitored budget expenditure through video conferencing for the past two months. This not only accelerated development works but also ensured the timely and proper utilisation of funds. Most is spent on bridge construction The department had set an ambitious target for the financial year 2025-26 to construct, reconstruct, strengthen, and develop 3,235 bridges. This includes work under NABARD, State Plan (Rural), and State Plan (Urban) schemes. These bridges are primarily being built in densely populated areas to facilitate smooth traffic flow from villages to cities. Additionally, under the 'Setu Bandhan' scheme, work is underway on the construction of 10 large bridges at a cost of 1,111 crore. These bridges are expected to reduce traffic congestion and improve connectivity. The construction of 18 new small bridges has been approved in the Devipatan division. Road development and other works The department has constructed 50 km-long model roads, built with road safety audits and widening, keeping future needs in mind. Modern facilities and safety standards have been implemented on these roads. The department has carried out road repairs, double-divider roads, and new construction works in several assembly constituencies based on proposals from MLAs. 1,253 crore rupees were spent on widening 33 roads to connect industrial parks. Meanwhile, the department repaired several state highways, such as Hamirpur-Rath and Gola-Shahjahanpur. 36,000 crore budget to be spent in 2026-27 The department has released a budget of 36,000 crore for the next financial year. In this, incomplete proposals from MLAs have been prioritised. It also includes 6 new highways and road-bridge works. These schemes are based on Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's vision of 'better connectivity from village to city'.

stories.title: CM instructs officials to complete works before monsoon arrival:Yogi reviews the progress of ongoing construction projects in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath, who arrived in Gorakhpur on a two-day tour, instructed the officials that most of the construction project work should be completed before the rains. He reviewed the progress of construction projects being conducted in the district with officials at Gorakhnath Temple. The CM said that all works should be expedited and full attention should be paid to quality. The CM said that projects that are more than two-thirds complete should be finished before the monsoon arrives. CM may propose new commercial complex The CM obtained information about the Bandhu Singh Park and Multi-level Parking cum Commercial Complex being built near Ghanta Ghar. He gave indications that during his next visit, he may inaugurate this and lay the foundation stone for the proposed new commercial complex for traders of the heritage corridor. Every project should meet its deadline The CM took information about the updated progress of all major development projects under construction in the district and metropolis. While reviewing, the Chief Minister said that every development project has a fixed timeline and it should be ensured that it is completed in a quality manner within that period itself. CM also warned that there should be no indifference or negligence at any level in this. It must be understood practically that when the rainy season begins, construction work in the open gets affected, therefore whatever development projects are underway, most of the construction work related to them should be completed before the rains. There is still time before the rainy season begins- CM In the review meeting, CM Yogi said that there is still time before the rainy season begins, but it must be ensured in time that waterlogging does not occur anywhere when it rains. Very good work has been done in the past few years to eliminate the problem of waterlogging, and it needs to be continuously taken towards excellence. While directing to complete the cleaning work of all drains in time, CM Yogi said that to eliminate the problem of waterlogging, serious attention should be paid to the Godhoiya drain project and efforts should be made to complete it soon. Got info about the progress of the Heritage Corridor construction Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath obtained information about the progress of the Heritage Corridor construction, the updated status of the multi-level parking cum commercial complex being built at Bandhu Singh Park located at Ghanta Ghar. He also inquired about the work plan for the new commercial complex to be built in Pandeyhata. He directed the Municipal Commissioner to keep complete preparations for inauguration and foundation stone laying at their level. CM Yogi, while emphasizing on the systematic rehabilitation of street vendors, also gave instructions that street traders should be given respectable space and complete facilities in the vending zone.

stories.title: SP leader assaults student after asking his caste at BHU:Victim files complaint, police search for accused
stories.summary: A student studying in the Hindi Department of Banaras Hindu University has submitted a complaint letter to the Chief Security Officer, making serious allegations. The case involves accusations of assault, using caste-based slurs, and death threats. Now know what the matter is Prashant Mishra, a second-year MA Hindi student, stated in his complaint that on Wednesday, around 11:45 AM, he arrived at the department for class. During this time, Himanshu Yadav, the unit president of Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, asked him about his name, caste, and course. According to the student, after providing the information, when he also asked Himanshu Yadav about his course, the accused became agitated. The complaint alleges that after this, Himanshu Yadav publicly abused and slapped the student. Not only that, but he also used caste-based derogatory words and threatened to kill him. This entire incident is reportedly recorded in the CCTV cameras installed in the department. Case registered at Lanka Police Station After receiving the application letter from the student, the Proctorial Department forwarded it to Lanka Police Station. In this matter, based on the complaint of Prashant Mishra, the police have registered a case against Himanshu Yadav under BNS sections 115(2), 352, 351(3). The police have stated that after registering the case, the accused student is being searched for and will be arrested soon. Meanwhile, the student has requested the Proctorial Department that he be provided protection from ragging and justice in this matter so that such an incident does not happen to him again.

stories.title: “Housing for every needy,” says CM Yogi:Hears 100 people at Gorakhpur Janata Darshan; assures financial aid for medical treatment
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath met people and listened to their problems during a Janta Darshan at Gorakhnath Temple on Thursday morning. He assured that every needy person would get housing and financial help for serious medical treatment. He said the government is committed to helping all eligible people and solving their problems. Around 100 people attended the Janta Darshan. The Chief Minister went to them, listened carefully, and took their applications. He sent their complaints to concerned officials and told them to solve all issues quickly, fairly, and properly. He also ordered strict action in police-related matters. A woman raised a housing issue during the event. The Chief Minister assured her that she would get a house under the government scheme. He also told people seeking help for serious illnesses that their treatment would not stop due to lack of money. Officials were instructed to quickly prepare estimates for expensive treatments and provide help without delay. During the event, the Chief Minister also gave chocolates to children who came with women and encouraged them to study well. CM Yogi paid heartfelt tributes to Markandey Yadav Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has expressed deep condolences on the demise of Markandey Yadav, an ardent devotee of Gorakshpeeth, a senior social worker, and a resident of Luhsi village in Pipraich. The Chief Minister reached his ancestral home in Luhsi on Thursday morning, offered a wreath on the mortal remains, and paid his heartfelt tributes. Markandey Yadav passed away on Wednesday morning during treatment at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram. He had immense devotion towards Gorakshpeeth. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reached the residence of Markandey Yadav in Luhsi on Thursday morning around 10:15 AM. He offered flowers and a wreath on the picture of the departed's mortal remains and paid heartfelt tributes. Expressing his deep condolences to the family, the Chief Minister prayed to Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath for the eternal peace of the departed soul. CM Yogi affectionately spoke to the family members of the late Markandey Yadav, including his wife Guddi Yadav 'Lakshmi', sons Sanjeev Yadav and Vishal Yadav, brother Harendra Yadav, daughter Vandana Yadav, son-in-law Himanshu Yadav, and consoled them. On this occasion, Gorakhpur Mayor Dr. Manglesh Srivastava, BJP State Vice President and MLC Dr. Dharmendra Singh, MLAs Mahendrapal Singh, Vipin Singh, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Village Development Bank Santraj Yadav, BJP District President Janardan Tiwari, Pipraich Nagar Panchayat Chairman Sanjay Maddheshiya, senior leaders Radheshyam Singh, Anand Shahi, Ranvijay Singh Munna, among others, were also present.

stories.title: Students shave heads at UP College in Varanasi:Sit on indefinite dharna in Surya Pratap murder case, demand action against principal
stories.summary: At the dharna site in UP (Uday Pratap) College in Varanasi, several students shaved their heads on Thursday. After this, they are sitting on dharna within the college campus itself. The agitated students who are protesting are demonstrating against the college principal in a unique manner. Meanwhile, more than 200 police force personnel are deployed at the dharna site on campus. ADCP Neetu Katyayan herself has reached the spot. A student was murdered in broad daylight on March 20 On March 20, student Surya Pratap Singh was murdered in broad daylight on the college campus. In this case, the main accused Manjeet Chauhan was arrested by the police on the same day. While the second accused Anuj surrendered in court on Tuesday. Students are continuously holding a front against the principal as well. They are also demanding that the accused be hanged as soon as possible. These students are sitting on an indefinite dharna demanding that a case be registered against the principal and that he be relieved from the college. 'Manjit, the murderer, should get death penalty' The students who got their heads shaved say that on March 20, Surya Pratap was murdered among 5000 students. The entire incident is recorded in CCTV. Despite this, no special action has been taken so far. The students are demanding that the accused student Manjeet should be hanged. Along with this, action should also be taken against the college principal, whose role is suspicious. An FIR should be registered against them and they should be immediately removed from the college. The protesting students say that until our demands are met, we will continue to sit in dharna protest.

Earlier, the businessman arrived in Ayodhya on Thursday morning at 8:30 AM with his wife and other family members. They landed at Maharishi Valmiki International Airport from Ahmedabad on 2 chartered flights. They proceeded directly to Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple with a long convoy. stories.title: MBA student who sold kidney cries before girlfriend:Pleads with police to not inform his mother; Kanpur kidney trafficking racket busted
stories.summary: Ayush, who sold his kidney for the lure of money in Kanpur, is admitted to the ICU of Hallet Hospital. The police asked Ayush to inform his family. At this, Ayush grabbed the feet of the policemen and started crying. He said, "Sir, don't tell my mother anything. I came to Kanpur saying I was going to work." The police say that after this, Ayush connected us with his girlfriend, who lives in Begusarai, Bihar. She came to Kanpur to meet Ayush. As soon as he saw his girlfriend, tears welled up in Ayush's eyes. He started crying inconsolably. He said, "I made a very big mistake." His girlfriend stroked his head and consoled him. Ayush, an MBA student trapped in the clutches of the kidney gang doctors in Kanpur, sold his kidney. Even after this, when he didn't receive the money, he exposed the matter. After the kidney removal, his health is not completely fine. He has been kept under the supervision of a medical team. Ayush is from Samastipur, Bihar, and the girl is from Begusarai. After arresting 6 people and sending them to jail, the police have issued a lookout notice against four absconding doctors associated with this gang. A team has left for Meerut. The police have received important input from there. Girlfriend asked Ayush - Why did you donate your kidney after all? Actually, after the raid in the kidney donation case, the police admitted Ayush to the ICU on the 6th floor of the Super Speciality at Hallet Hospital. On Wednesday afternoon, around 12 o'clock, Ayush's girlfriend was allowed to meet him under strict police security. After reaching Kanpur from Bihar, she was guarded by three male sub-inspectors, one female sub-inspector, and one constable from Rawatpur police station. Three sub-inspectors were with Ayush's girlfriend in the ICU, while two policemen were present below PGI. The girlfriend stroked his head, comforting him and wiping his tears. The girl asked Ayush - Why did you donate a kidney after all? To which he said that he was unable to collect money for fees. Because of this, he had been troubled for two months. During this time, he met Shivam Agarwal, and influenced by his words, he underwent a kidney transplant. Girlfriend said - Ayush's mother is worried Ayush's girlfriend expressed her displeasure with him. At this, Ayush tried to get up from the bed by holding her hand, but could not due to pain. The girl inquired about Ayush's health from the doctors and hospital staff. During this, she told Ayush that his mother was very upset. She was asking him to come with her. She told the police that Ayush also has a younger brother named Rishabh. He works a private job. After staying in the ICU for about an hour, as soon as she came out, she was surrounded by media personnel. After this, she went back into the ICU. Then police personnel escorted her out through the hospital's back gate. The girlfriend studies at the same Graphic Era University in Dehradun where Ayush studies. She is in the second semester, while Ayush is in the fourth semester. Parul's brother sat outside the ICU all day Vikas Tomar, husband of receiver Parul Tomar, a resident of Meerut, did not reach Kanpur on Wednesday. Police officials spoke to him over the phone. On Wednesday, Parul's brother Divyank came to Kanpur. He is a resident of Dholpur, Bijnor. He sat outside the ICU on the 6th floor of Hallet's Super Specialty PGI all day with a bag. He was not allowed to meet her. He said that Dr. Afzal had brought his sister to Kanpur for a kidney transplant. How much money was given for the kidney donation? To this question, he said that his brother-in-law had given the money, "we don't know." After that, he refused to answer any further questions. Ayush told the police - This is how he got trapped in the gang's clutches DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said that Ayush Kumar is now in a condition to talk. He was interrogated on Wednesday. According to the DCP, Ayush said that the kidney deal was struck for 6 lakh rupees. Half the money was to be paid in cash and the rest was to be deposited in the account after the operation. After the operation, only three and a half lakh rupees were deposited in the account. According to Ayush, first he came into contact with a person named Ali. He made him talk to Dr. Anurag alias Amit. After this, he spoke with Dr. Vaibhav. Then he introduced him to Dr. Afzal. Dr. Afzal asked for Ayush's complete medical report. After that, he introduced him to agent Shivam. Shivam sent this complete report to Dr. Rohit in Noida. It was only at Dr. Rohit's insistence that the operation was decided to be performed at Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur. Ayush came to Kanpur only after everything was finalized. Dr. Afzal runs Alpha Hospital in Meerut According to the DCP, Dr. Afzal is the operator of Alpha Hospital in Meerut. Besides Dr. Afzal, Dr. Vaibhav and Dr. Anurag alias Amit are also residents of Meerut. That's why a team has been sent to Meerut to search for them. Shivam's call details are being extracted to trace Dr. Rohit. A lookout notice has been issued to prevent these people from fleeing the country. He stated that Ayush claims an 8-doctor team came to Ahuja Hospital in two cars. In one car, there were 5 people including Dr. Afzal, Dr. Vaibhav, and Dr. Anurag. While 3 people were present in the second car. Based on the numbers found in the CCTV footage, the investigation progressed, and the police found out that one car had left for Lucknow and the other for Ghaziabad. In Ghaziabad, the fare was transferred to the taxi driver via UPI. After this, the entire medical staff, including the doctors, switched off their mobiles. DCP West stated that police teams are engaged in Lucknow, Ghaziabad, and Noida in search of the accused. Arrests are likely by late night. Ayush pleaded - Sir, please help me get the remaining money. Ayush Kumar, a resident of Samastipur, Bihar, informed the police about his family's financial situation. He said - the family land is mortgaged. Because of this, he couldn't get a loan. He also got caught in the trap of cybercriminals. He had opened a mule account at their behest. The cybercriminals had promised to give him 20 thousand rupees, but they didn't give that either. With his father gone, the family's situation is dire. He had decided to sell his kidney so that his studies wouldn't stop, but he wasn't given the money for that either. He folded his hands and pleaded with the police officers to help him get the remaining amount. Police picked up 3 suspects After arresting 6 people in the illegal kidney transplant case in Kanpur, the police are now searching for four absconding individuals. A lookout notice has been issued against all of them. A police team has gone to Meerut to apprehend the absconding doctors. In this whole racket, the police are looking for Dr Afzal, the owner of Alpha Hospital, along with Dr. Rohit alias Rahul, Dr. Vaibhav, and Dr. Anurag alias Amit. Police investigation has revealed that more than 100 transplants have been performed at Alpha Hospital in Meerut. The director of this hospital is Dr. Afzal, who is absconding in the kidney scam. Therefore, the police are searching for him. Following this, a team has departed for Meerut. Additionally, on Wednesday, the police took 3 suspects into custody. DCP West MA Qasim Abidi stated - Agent Shivam Agarwal revealed during interrogation that Dr Afzal has confessed to illegally performing kidney transplants in his own hospital. It has also come to light during the investigation that Ahuja Hospital, belonging to Dr Preeti Ahuja, Vice President of IMA Kanpur, was registered in September 2025, whereas several transplants were performed at the hospital even before its registration.

stories.title: Bulldozers used on mosque in Lucknow at night:Built on government land, action taken on Allahabad High Court orders
stories.summary: A mosque built on Gram Sabha land in Lucknow was demolished at night. This action was taken after the order of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court. On the sixth day of the order, it was razed to the ground in the presence of tehsil-level officials. Heavy police force remained deployed during this time. At 3 AM on Wednesday night, 3 bulldozers arrived to demolish the mosque. This case relates to the land of Gata number 648 located in village Asti of BKT tehsil, on which the mosque was constructed. The concerned party could not prove any valid right over the land in the High Court. Following this, the order to demolish was given, upholding the previous orders of the Tehsildar and Additional District Magistrate (Judicial). See 3 pictures- 3 bulldozers arrived at 3 AM At 3 AM, police and tehsil-level officials arrived with 3 bulldozers. According to officials, after the High Court's order, a notice to remove the mosque had been pasted on its wall. After that, the given time was waited for. Despite that, the illegally built structure did not move, so the administration had it removed. High Court upheld the Tehsil's order According to Tehsildar Sharad Kumar, Mohammad Sahibaan and Lal Mohammad of Asti village were served notices after the High Court's order. It stated that a mosque was built on government threshing ground. The same was stated at the tehsil level as well. They were ordered to remove the illegal structure from there and were fined 36 thousand rupees. Then these people, not complying with the order, approached the High Court. They did not get any relief from there either. The High Court also upheld the tehsil level order and said that there was no error in the measurement. The structure is built on government land. However, the High Court granted the relief that the fine of 36 thousand rupees was waived. The action lasted for about 1 hour According to ADM Administration Rakesh Singh, upon receiving information about the action at night, there was news of resistance from the encroachers. Upon this, an inspection was carried out on the spot with the SDM. After taking stock, the administration gave a clear warning that illegal encroachment would be removed at all costs. Any kind of obstruction to law and order would not be tolerated. After this, at 3 AM, they reached the spot with PAC forces. After taking stock there, 3 bulldozers were deployed. In the action that lasted for about 1 hour, the entire mosque was razed to the ground. No obstruction was encountered during this action. The Gram Samaj land has been freed from encroachment and cleared. Now the villagers will be able to set up threshing floors there again. Administration had been accused of encroachment The administration alleged that the mosque was illegally constructed by encroaching upon this very land. On the other hand, the encroachers stated that the mosque was built about 60 years ago by the local Muslim community and it was not a new encroachment. They also argued that they only go there to offer prayers and have no connection with the management of the mosque. Additionally, the encroachers questioned the hearing process, stating that they were not given the opportunity to cross-examine witnesses. The court clarified that under Section 67 of the UP Revenue Code, proceedings in such cases are conducted through a summary procedure, where decisions can be made based on affidavits. Cross-examination of witnesses is not mandatory in every case. The court found that the land belonged to the Gram Sabha and the encroachers could not prove any valid right, ownership, or interest over it. On this basis, the eviction order was deemed correct. High Court had given the order 6 days ago The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court upheld the Tehsildar's eviction order from a mosque built on Gram Sabha land, considering it correct. The court had stated that there was no error either in the Tehsildar's order or in the Additional District Magistrate's order dismissing the appeal. However, the court quashed the fine of Rs 36,000 imposed on the petitioners. The court found that the petitioners had no role in constructing the mosque on this land, which was recorded as a threshing floor. This decision was passed by the single bench of Justice Alok Mathur on a petition filed by Shahban and others. The petitioners had challenged the orders passed by the Tehsildar and the Additional District Magistrate (Judicial).

stories.title: Rain and hail alert in UP from tomorrow:Storm warning issued, crop losses reported; Yogi directs DMs to ensure farmers face no trouble
stories.summary: The weather in UP is going to change again. From tomorrow, i.e., Friday, a spell of unseasonal rain will begin once again. According to the Meteorological Department, there will be heavy rain in the state. During this period, lightning and hailstones may fall. Storms with speeds of 50 to 60 KM per hour may occur. Currently, the weather has been clear since Thursday morning. Bright sunshine has spread across the entire state. A light cool breeze is blowing. Before this, unseasonal rain occurred in different parts over the past 2 days. Kannauj received the highest rainfall at 29 mm, Mainpuri at 20 mm, and Lucknow at 15.1 mm. 10 mm of rain was recorded in Etah, Hathras, and Chitrakoot. Hailstones also fell in many places along with strong winds. Unseasonal rain and strong winds have caused significant damage to crops. CM Yogi inquired about the condition of farmers affected by unseasonal rain on Wednesday. He sought reports from officials. He instructed all District Magistrates to remain on alert mode. He said - farmers should not face any kind of trouble. Assess crop damage and ensure farmers receive compensation soon. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Singh said - The weather in UP is going to change once again from April 3. Two consecutive western disturbances are becoming active on April 3 and 7. Its greater impact will be seen in Western Uttar Pradesh, Madhyanchal, and Bundelkhand. Due to the activity of the western disturbance, strong winds will blow. Rain and hailstones will fall. There will be a drop of 5C in temperature. View weather pictures- How will the weather be for 5 days? Condition of Major Cities Farmers said - The ripe crops were ruined Crops of 15 thousand farmers damaged in 15 days According to the UP government, 4300 hectares of crops belonging to 15 thousand farmers have been damaged in the last 15 days. So far, 10,278 farmers have received compensation.

stories.title: 60-foot swing collapsed, 30 injured:2 children critical; eyewitness says it spun twice before breaking
stories.summary: A major accident occurred at 11:30 PM on Wednesday night at the Bhaisaha fair in Kushinagar, UP. A 60-foot swing installed at the fair uprooted and fell while rotating. Around 20 to 30 people were injured. The condition of 2 children is said to be serious. After the accident, there was chaos at the scene. Amidst screams, people rushed to help. According to eyewitnesses, about 80 people were on the swing at the time of the accident. After rotating 3-4 times, the swing started creaking. People shouted, but the operator ignored them. Shortly after, the swing broke with a loud noise. People sitting on it fell down. People were trapped underneath as the swing fell on them. Police personnel deployed at the fair started rescue operations with the help of nearby people. People were pulled out and taken to the hospital. Here, injured Lalu Gupta said, 'When we got on the swing, there was a rattling sound, but no one paid attention. Then the swing rotated twice and then suddenly broke.' The incident is from Khadda police station area. A four-day Bhaisaha fair is ongoing here since March 30. Apart from Purvanchal, a large number of people from Nepal and Bihar also come to the fair. The fair was very crowded since Wednesday evening. See the accident in pictures More than 10 people were referred to the medical college According to the police, people standing near the swing were also caught in the accident. Many people were trapped under the swing. Some shops were also affected. After the accident, local residents joined the rescue efforts. They joined the police at the fair in rescuing people. People trapped under the swing were somehow pulled out. All the injured were sent to the hospital in 6 ambulances. More than 10 people were referred to the medical college. MLA Arrived Upon Receiving Information of the Incident Khadda MLA Vivekananda Pandey reached the spot upon receiving information about the incident. He said, The swing had fallen in the fair. All injured people were taken to the hospital. Some people were treated locally. Seriously injured were sent to the district hospital. Officials are making every possible effort to ensure everyone receives proper medical treatment. We pray to God that everyone recovers quickly. Suspicion of Negligence in Swing Operation The Bhaisaha Fair is held every year on Chaitra Purnima near the ancient Durga Temple, located on the banks of the Narayani River. stories.title: Criminal seeking extortion of ₹5 Cr shot dead in encounter:Had ₹50,000 reward in Moradabad; linked to 36 cases including murder and robbery
stories.summary: On Wednesday night, police shot dead a criminal who had demanded 5 crore rupees from a businessman. Ashu, also known as Monty, was a skilled shooter in the Udham Singh gang. He had 33 cases against him, including murder and robbery. The encounter happened near the post-mortem house in the Civil Lines area. Ashu was on the run in an extortion case. Police had also announced a reward of 50 thousand rupees for his capture. Officers had been raiding different places to catch him. Acting on a tip-off, police cordoned off the Civil Lines area. When Ashu saw them near the post-mortem house, he tried to flee on a bike and opened fire. Police returned fire, hitting him twice. One bullet struck his chest, killing him instantly. Another criminal escaped in the darkness. Police are searching for him. Udham Singh, a notorious criminal from West UP, had been released on bail from jail on March 26 after more than four years. After his release, Meerut police issued alerts, keeping police across West UP on high alert. How he came in contact with Udham Singh In 2010, Ashu Chadha alias Monty went to jail in a murder case. While in jail, he came in contact with members of the notorious Udham Singh gang. After coming out, he became an active member of this gang. After getting bail, he continuously started committing incidents of robbery and murder. Due to this, cases were registered against him in several police stations of Western Uttar Pradesh. Exports home decor items to foreign countries Arshu Dhal, a resident of Shubham Green Villa, has a firm named Wazirchand Exports. He exports brass, glass, and wooden home decor items to more than 125 countries. Arshu told the police- On the night of March 12, around 8 PM, I received a missed call on my mobile from an unknown number. Approximately one minute later, a call came again on WhatsApp. When I received the call, the person on the other end started abusing. After this, I disconnected the call. A little later, the accused sent a message on WhatsApp saying to quickly arrange five crore rupees. On March 14, around 2:30 PM, the accused WhatsApped again and threatened, "You don't know Udham Singh. If the money is not given, we will kill you." The very next day, bike-borne miscreants reached the gate of my factory and opened fire. Guard had filed FIR for firing After the firing incident, security guard Umesh filed a complaint at the Civil Lines police station. SSP Moradabad Satpal Antil was previously posted in Meerut. Because of this, he knew well about the Udham Singh gang. He deployed 5 teams to trace the gang. Ashu was out on bail Ashu alias Monty, a resident of Mirapur village in Hapur district's Hafizpur police station area, had recently been released from jail on bail. He had been absconding since then. Police were continuously searching for him. Around 9 PM on Wednesday night, Ashu reached near Arshu Dhal in Moradabad to collect extortion money. As soon as he reached near the post-mortem house, the police surrounded him. Seeing himself surrounded, Ashu started firing at the police. In retaliatory firing by the police, Ashu sustained two bullet injuries, one of which hit him in the chest. He fell on the spot. Police immediately took him to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. 260 criminals killed in encounters in 8 years According to the state government, from March 2017 to October 2025, UP Police have killed 260 criminals in encounters. During this period, more than 15,000 police encounters took place, in which over 31,000 criminals were arrested and more than 10,000 were shot.
