stories.title: 4 terrorists arrested in Lucknow over blast plot:Gang leader from Meerut; Pakistan-based handlers assigned targets for attacks
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested four suspected terrorists in Lucknow, officials confirmed on Friday. According to the ATS, the group was allegedly planning arson and terror attacks across India under the direction of handlers based in Pakistan. The accused have been identified as Saqib alias Devil, Vikas Gehlawat alias Raunak, Lokesh alias Babu, also known as Papla Pandit, and Arbab. Saqib is believed to be the leader of the group. From their possession, ATS recovered a chemical-filled container, seven mobile phones, 24 pamphlets, and Aadhaar cards. Investigators are analysing key digital evidence found on the seized devices. Plan to target Lucknow Railway Station The ATS revealed that the group had planned to target infrastructure near Lucknow Railway Station, including damaging the railway signal box. The intention was to trigger a major explosion and cause significant casualties on 2 April, thereby spreading panic. Acting on prior intelligence, ATS teams intervened in time and apprehended the suspects before the plan could be executed. Links to Pakistan and foreign networks Preliminary investigation indicates that the group was in contact with Pakistani handlers through social media and encrypted communication platforms. Saqib, a resident of Agwanpur village in Meerut who worked as a barber, is said to have established these connections. He reportedly communicated with handlers via platforms such as Telegram, Instagram, and Signal. Authorities also found links to suspicious foreign numbers, including some believed to be based in Afghanistan. These platforms were allegedly used for secure coordination of anti-national activities. Network built through local recruitment Investigators said Saqib expanded the network by recruiting acquaintances. He first involved Arbab, who is from his village, and later brought in Vikas Gehlawat and Lokesh, both residents of Gautam Buddh Nagar, through online contact. Officials believe that financial incentives and exposure to radical content motivated the accused to join the network. The group had reportedly been conducting reconnaissance at various locations. Reconnaissance and target identification The primary objective of the group was to create fear and instability. For this purpose, they carried out reconnaissance of key locations, including prominent institutions, crowded public areas, vehicles, and railway infrastructure. Cities such as Ghaziabad, Aligarh, and Lucknow were among the locations surveyed. Pakistani handlers allegedly shared specific locations via Google Maps, which the accused would visit and document through videos before sending detailed reports back. Use of arson and financial incentives During interrogation, it emerged that the accused carried out small-scale arson incidents to demonstrate their activities. These acts were recorded and shared with handlers in Pakistan as proof. In return, payments were reportedly made through QR code-based transactions. Authorities believe this financial arrangement played a role in sustaining the network’s operations. Radicalisation and intent to disrupt peace Investigators also found that the accused were exposed to radical ideologies through online groups linked to extremist organisations. They were allegedly encouraged to carry out acts of violence and arson in the name of religion. According to the ATS, the overarching aim was to spread fear, fuel communal tension, and disrupt internal peace and security across the country.

stories.title: First N-Gen Post Office opens in Varanasi:Cafe-like feel and digital services at one place give full comfort
stories.summary: The N-Gen (Next Generation) Post Office has been inaugurated at the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith campus in Varanasi. This is the first N-Gen Post Office in the Varanasi region, which has been designed keeping in mind the needs of youth and students. It was inaugurated by the university's Vice-Chancellor Professor Anand Kumar Tyagi and Postmaster General Padmagandha Mishra. The interior of this N-Gen has been designed in a cafe style, providing facilities to sit and work and spend time. Options like a mini library, TV, video games, chess and carrom are also available for students. Additionally, free Wi-Fi facility has been provided so that students can easily do their studies and other online work. The walls and seating arrangement have been designed in such a way that this place looks less like an official office and more like a youth zone. Here, along with postal services, facilities of digital banking, e-commerce logistics and India Post Payments Bank are also available at one place. This means if a student needs to send money, open an account or get information related to online orders, there is no need to go to different places. During the inauguration, Postmaster General Padmagandha Mishra said that this initiative has been started keeping youth in mind, so that they can connect with new technology along with postal services. Vice Chancellor Professor Anand Kumar Tyagi said that with the start of such a facility in the university, the connection between students and the postal department will be strengthened and they will get the benefit of new facilities. Khushi Rai, a BA third-year student at Kashi Vidyapeeth, appreciated this initiative and said that this post office is very useful for students. She mentioned that the atmosphere here is very good and students can sit here and get information related to their postal and banking needs, among other requirements. According to students, this N-Gen Post Office has now emerged as a new center of new facilities, better services and modern environment for the youth.

stories.title: No one can read namaz on roads':UP CM Yogi says in Asam rally, 'Rioters' property is distributed among poor'
stories.summary: 'We used to say that Ram Lalla, we will come and build the temple there. Congress said that Ram never existed. Congress's allies worked to deny Ram's existence. But under the BJP's double-engine government, a grand Ram temple has been constructed in Ayodhya. Now, there is no curfew in UP. No curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. No one can offer namaz on the streets. There is no sound of shouting from any religion. If anyone dares to riot, their property is confiscated and distributed among the poor and Dalits.' These statements were made by CM Yogi on Friday during the assembly election campaign in Assam. He had arrived to hold a rally in support of NDA candidate Deepak Kumar Das for the Barpeta assembly seat. 1. 'Congress allies worked to deny Ram's existence' Yogi said that the double-engine government respects heritage. Only a double-engine government can do this. Wherever there is a BJP government, work has been shown. There was a movement for Shri Ram Janmabhoomi in Ayodhya; people used to come from Assam too. We used to say that we would come to Ramlala, we would build the temple there. Congress used to say that Ram never existed. Congress allies have worked to deny Ram's existence. But, under the BJP's double-engine government, a grand Ram temple has been constructed in Ayodhya. 2. 'Will not let the conspiracy of Congress and UDF succeed' The CM said that Congress and UDF tampered with the culture of Assam. They worked to spoil the demography here by infiltrating infiltrators. They attempted to forcibly occupy the houses and land of the people of Assam. On one hand, the government under the leadership of Himanta Biswa Sarma is working to advance development and heritage. Arrangements are also being made to identify each and every infiltrator and remove them from here. On the other hand, major development works are also being witnessed in Assam. It is the resolve of NDA that we will not let Assam become a land of land jihad and love jihad; we will not let infiltration happen here. We will not let the conspiracy of Congress and UDF succeed. 3. UP is riot-free, curfew-free, mafia-free Yogi said - I have come specially from UP to say this, that not a single riot has occurred in UP in nine years. UP is riot-free, curfew-free, mafia-free, and development work is happening in full swing. 4. 'Congress has insulted India and Indian values' Yogi said that the double-engine government has decided that Assam will not be allowed to become a part of infiltration. Infiltrators will be removed and thrown out. Whenever Congress or UDF people have had an opportunity, they have continuously insulted India, and Indian values. UDF is the mother of infiltration in Assam; it gives shelter to infiltrators. It wants to capture the government in Assam on their strength. Congress wants to destroy Assam's culture by joining hands with them. However, the NDA's double-engine government is working to remove each and every infiltrator while securing and protecting Assam's cultural heritage.

stories.title: Minors involved in Agra nude video scandal were friends:Aged between 14-17; boys sent to juvenile home, girls undergoing counselling
stories.summary: The Khandoli area of Agra suddenly came into focus on March 31 after 48 obscene videos were circulated on social media. The clips showed three boys and two girls, all aged between 14 and 17. The videos went viral at a time when the Shri Ram fair was underway in the area, leading to tension. Although no formal complaint was filed, police took cognisance and arrested two boys. During the probe, it emerged that the girls belong to Hindu families, while one of the boys is Muslim. Following this, 48 police personnel were deployed in the area. All those involved are minors, so police are proceeding cautiously. The arrested boys have been sent to a juvenile home, while both girls are undergoing counselling. It has come to light that all five knew each other and whatever is seen in the videos was consensual. Questions have arisen over how the videos suddenly surfaced, why they were made, who leaked them and what options the police now have. Minister inaugurated the fair, obscene videos spread at the fair Khandoli is located around 20 km from the Agra district headquarters. The 126th historic Shri Ram fair and wrestling event is currently underway there. It was inaugurated on March 26 by Union Minister of State Prof SP Singh Baghel. Until then, the fair was the main attraction, but the situation changed on March 31. Videos began circulating among people at the fair. The clips showed two girls and three boys in an explicit state. By 9 am, the videos had started spreading rapidly, and by noon, they had reached almost everyone in the area. Locals identified the boys in the videos as residents of the same village. One boy is Muslim, while the others belong to Maurya and Kashyap communities. Of the two girls seen in the videos, one belongs to the Thakur community and the other to the OBC category. Both are from different villages. All were studying in classes 9 to 12, except the Muslim boy, who had dropped out and was working at a shop. Friendship through social media, then started meeting each other Residents of the villages said the group already knew each other and later connected on Instagram, where they used to communicate. They exchanged photos and videos. Being young, they engaged in showing off, forming relationships and recording videos. They were often seen roaming together in the locality. Planned to meet 3 months ago, then made nude videos The sequence began around three months ago when the five planned to meet. They chose a friend’s house as the location and gathered there. At the house, they recorded explicit videos. No force or coercion is visible in the clips. Some videos are around 30 seconds long, while others are 10–15 seconds. Two girls and two boys are seen in compromising acts, while the third boy recorded the videos. Where the incident occurred, there have been disturbances before as well Locals said the area has a significant Thakur population and has witnessed disputes earlier. After the incident, tension increased, prompting the administration to go on alert and deploy police. One reason cited is that one of the accused boys belongs to the Muslim community and appears in the videos. Movement near his house has been restricted. After the videos surfaced, families of those involved confined themselves indoors. No one lodged a complaint, but police understood the seriousness and registered an FIR on their own, arresting two boys. Station House Officer Kuldeep Singh said that if the girls’ families file a complaint, further charges will be added. For now, an FIR has been registered under sections related to uploading obscene content on digital platforms. Sold the mobile, that's why the videos came out During questioning, one of the boys told police that the videos were stored on his phone, which he later sold without deleting the data, leading to their circulation. However, he could not clearly explain when and to whom the phone was sold. His statements also contained contradictions. He also failed to explain what other data was stored on the device. Police suspect there may be more to the case. Two different locations are visible in the videos, suggesting they may have been recorded at separate places. There are 6 more questions before the police, which are being investigated... DCP said- Appeal to people, don't share these videos DCP of Agra West, Aditya Singh said- All the boys and girls involved in this are minors. The videos that are currently going viral are all from 3 months ago. Two boys have been arrested so far. During interrogation, it was also revealed that all of them were previously acquainted with each other. The DCP also appealed to people that if you have the video, do not share it. Action can be taken for sharing it.

stories.title: Woman who robbed jewellery shop in Ayodhya in Burqa arrested:Turns out to be Hindu girl; 4-month-old pregnant lady used fake gun for robbery
stories.summary: Police in Ayodhya have arrested a 25-year-old woman and her 27-year-old accomplice late on Thursday night for carrying out a robbery at a jewellery shop while disguised in a burqa. The accused have been identified as Payal and her friend Rahul, who was waiting on a motorcycle some distance away during the incident. Payal fled the scene and escaped with Rahul. Police investigation revealed that Rahul had purchased a fake pistol and a burqa from the market. Payal reached the shop around 12:30 pm wearing the burqa and used the fake weapon to rob a gold necklace and chain worth around ₹3.6 lakh. The duo had planned the crime using the burqa to conceal identity. The incident took place in the Kothi Bazaar area under Rudauli police station limits. The entire act was captured on six CCTV cameras installed at the shop. The registration number of the motorcycle used in the escape was also recorded, which helped police trace and arrest both accused. ADG Zone Lucknow Praveen Kumar informed- Two people have been arrested. The name of the girl who committed the robbery wearing a burqa is Payal. The name of the boy who was with her is Rahul. Both were executing the incident by becoming Bunty and Babli. Both are friends. The robbery was carried out by showing a toy pistol. Now read the complete matter in detail... She came wearing a burqa to buy a gold necklace and chain Mahesh, a gold and silver trader from Kothi Bazaar, runs Mahesh Jewellers located about 900 metres from his residence in Agrawal Complex. On Thursday, Payal, a resident of Ahibaran ka Purwa in Mathana Nivada gram panchayat, arrived at the shop along with her friend Rahul from Paran ka Purwa village. Payal entered the shop alone wearing a burqa and carrying a backpack, while Rahul stayed back at a distance. She told Mahesh that she wanted to purchase a gold necklace and chain, following which he placed both items before her. She then asked for water. Mahesh sent his employee Ankit Kumar to bring water and samosas. After Ankit returned, Payal refused to eat the samosa but took the water bottle. Said - I don't eat samosas, please get me sweets Payal then said she does not eat samosas and asked for sweets. Mahesh sent Ankit again to bring barfi. During this time, another employee, Maniram, placed the necklace and chain on the counter. Payal stood up and started moving around inside the shop. When Mahesh asked her what she was looking for, she replied that her husband had gone to withdraw money and she was waiting for him. She then stood near the counter. As Mahesh got busy arranging other items in the cupboard, Payal picked up the gold necklace and chain from the box and lifted her bag. Pulled out pistol from waist, said- If you move forward, I will shoot When the shopkeeper tried to stop her, she pulled out a pistol from her waist, pointed it at him and threatened to shoot if he moved forward. She then ran out of the shop. Mahesh and Maniram chased her, raising an alarm. Payal ran on foot and escaped with Rahul, who was waiting on a motorcycle a short distance away. According to Mahesh, the necklace weighed 26 grams (22 carat) and was valued at around ₹3.6 lakh as per market rates on April 2. Know about the accused- Payal’s father, Ramkeval, runs a laundry centre named after her. She is the third among four sisters; the eldest is married, while the other two live at home. Rahul lives about 16 km away from Payal’s residence. Rahul, a resident of Paran ka Purwa in Nevra gram panchayat, had lost his father Radheshyam some time ago. He is the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother Lavkush stays at home, while another brother, Bablu, works as a labourer in Delhi. Rahul lives separately.

stories.title: Seema Haider names son ‘Bharat’:Says, 'Proud to be Hindu in India, do not want to return to Pakistan'
stories.summary: Seema Haider, who came to India from Pakistan, has named her newborn son ‘Bharat’. The naming ceremony was held on Thursday at her residence in Rabupura, Noida. Seema said Hinduism is very beautiful and she feels proud to be a Hindu. Seema Haider said- I support India in cricket matches. When India wins a match, I feel happy. During the match, I pray to God that India should win. The people of India are very good. I don't want to go back to Pakistan. People of every caste live here. They love me, respect me. They consider me their daughter-in-law. In fact, this is Seema Haider’s sixth child, whom she gave birth to on February 18, 2026, at a hospital in Noida. Earlier, she had also given birth to a daughter. Seema has four children from her Pakistani husband, while she has two children with her Indian husband Sachin Meena. When the priest suggested the name, it came with the letter ‘Bh’ Seema Haider said that when the priest suggested a name, it started with the letter ‘Bha’. After much thought, the name ‘Bharat’ was chosen. She said there could be no better name than Bharat. She added that she is very happy after coming to India and has never regretted leaving Pakistan. Seema has 2 million followers on YouTube channel- Seema creates videos with her husband Sachin. She has been living with him in Rabupura, Noida, since 2023. Their story has remained widely discussed. The couple is very active on social media. Their YouTube channel has more than 2 million followers. Love through PUBG game, came to India via Nepal Seema Haider married Ghulam Haider in 2014. In 2019, Ghulam Haider moved to Dubai, leaving Seema and their four children in Karachi. That same year, Seema met Sachin Meena from Rabupura, Noida, online while playing PUBG. On March 10, 2023, Seema and Sachin met in person in Nepal. They claimed to have converted religion and married in a temple there. After that, Seema returned to Pakistan while Sachin came back to Noida. On May 13, Seema again travelled from Pakistan to Nepal via Dubai and then reached Rabupura by bus. On July 1, Seema and Sachin met a lawyer in Bulandshahr to get Indian identity documents prepared. The lawyer informed the police about Seema being a Pakistani national. Sachin-Seema were taken into custody from Haryana After this, both went absconding. On July 3, Seema and Sachin were taken into custody from Ballabhgarh in Haryana. On July 4, 2023, Sachin’s father Netrapal was arrested by the police. On July 8, all three were granted bail by the court. On July 17 and 18, the ATS questioned Seema and Sachin. On July 21, 2023, photos and videos of their wedding surfaced. Filed petition with the President for citizenship On July 21, 2023, Seema filed a petition with the President seeking Indian citizenship. On July 23, after questioning Sachin’s cousin in Bulandshahr, two youths from Ahmedgarh were detained and later arrested. On July 30, 2023, Seema released a video appealing for help, saying she did not even have money for food. On August 2, filmmaker Amit Jani from Meerut announced a film titled ‘Karachi to Noida’ based on Seema and Sachin, and a promo shoot was done. However, the film has not been completed yet.

stories.title: Kanpur’s cross-border kidney transplant racket:African woman pays ₹2.5 Cr for surgery; several hospitals in spotlight
stories.summary: The Kanpur kidney transplant racket has links not only within Uttar Pradesh but also abroad. Foreign patients were secretly coming here for illegal kidney transplants. The traffickers had formed a panel of hospitals and doctors across several states, including Delhi, Mumbai and West Bengal, to carry out the operations. After finalising deals with both donors and recipients, the gang conducted illegal kidney transplants at different locations across the country. Which hospital would be used, which doctors’ team would perform the transplant, and who the donor and recipient were—everything was kept secret. Separate individuals handled each responsibility. The doctors’ team would arrive by flight, complete the transplant within a few hours, and leave. So far, 8 arrests have been made in the case. How the kidney transplant racket was operating and what its international links are—here is what the arrested OT technicians told. OT Technician Spills the Beans - Conducted Transplants in Several States Kanpur DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said that six accused have already been sent to jail. On April 2, two OT technicians—Kuldeep Singh Raghav and Rajesh Kumar—were arrested. Rajesh is a resident of Ghaziabad and works as an OT technician at Sarvodaya Hospital in Noida, while Kuldeep Singh Raghav is from Pilkhuwa in Hapur and works at Shanti Gopal Hospital. During questioning, both revealed that a doctor named Rohit from Noida used to send them for kidney transplant cases. Along with them, a urologist would also travel from Delhi to Kanpur by flight for the transplant. They were paid between ₹35,000 and ₹50,000 for each case. Transplant of South African Woman Performed According to DCP Qasim Abidi, the technicians revealed that they were involved not only in Kanpur cases but also in the transplant of a South African woman named Arabica. The gang carried out kidney transplants not only in Kanpur but also in Delhi, Meerut, Noida, West Bengal and Haryana. Doctor Rohit from Noida had created a panel of hospitals in every state. For example, in Kanpur alone, he had six hospitals in his panel. All operations in Kanpur and nearby districts were handled by Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada. Panel of 8 doctors, flight arrangements The gang had formed a panel of eight doctors. Wherever a transplant had to be carried out, Dr Rohit arranged flight travel for all of them. In Kanpur too, in a similar manner, on the night of March 29 at 9 pm, a kidney from Ayush was transplanted into Parul Tomar from Muzaffarnagar. Doctors would reach the concerned city directly by flight, perform the transplant, and then leave. Keeping Donor-Receiver Names Secret DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said the entire operation was run like a secret mission. The identities of the doctors performing the transplant, the donor and recipient, and the hospital where the transplant was to take place were all kept confidential. The entire work was handled by different teams. For example, Parul Tomar, a resident of North Civil Lines in Muzaffarnagar, had struck a deal with Dr Afzal from Meerut. Meanwhile, Ayush Kumar, an MBA student from Bihar studying in Dehradun, had finalised a deal to sell his kidney with Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada of Kanpur. Both were in contact with absconding Noida-based doctor Rohit. Foreigners' Kidneys Replaced for Up to 2.50 Crores According to the police, within India, kidney transplants were carried out for ₹60 lakh to ₹1 crore. However, foreign patients were charged up to ₹2.5 crore. Evidence has been found showing that the kidney transplant of the South African woman Arabica was done for ₹2 crore to ₹2.5 crore. The syndicate has carried out not just a few but hundreds of kidney transplants. More than 50 people, including brokers and doctors, are believed to be involved in this network. Police teams are conducting raids from Kanpur to Meerut, Lucknow, Delhi, Noida and Ghaziabad. Know About Police Action Kanpur Police have so far arrested 8 accused in this case. DCP West said that after the racket was exposed, CCTV footage of people visiting Ahuja Hospital on the night of March 29 was examined. Two cars were used to transport doctors—one carrying five doctors and the other three. Three doctors were dropped in Ghaziabad, while five were dropped in Lucknow. Police are also examining further CCTV footage. So far, the investigation has revealed that Noida-based Dr Rohit alias Rahul and three Meerut-based doctors—Dr Afzal, Dr Vaibhav and Dr Anurag alias Amit—are involved in the gang. All their names are mentioned in the FIR, and police teams are conducting raids to arrest them. Know about the Meerut hospital to which the links are being traced During the investigation of the Kanpur kidney case, it has emerged that more than 100 transplants were carried out at Alpha Hospital in Meerut. The hospital is located in Mangal Pandey Nagar and is built on about 350 square yards. The building has four floors. The director of the hospital is Amit Kumar. The hospital management and staff claim that no doctor named Afzal is associated with them. According to the manager, only regular OPD services by Dr Vaibhav Mugdal are conducted, while other doctors are called on demand. At present, police are questioning the manager and continuing the investigation. Alpha Hospital was in the news before as well Meanwhile, Meerut's CMO Dr. Ashok Kataria says that on November 26, 2025, a patient complained that he was admitted after taking commission. The hospital's license was suspended on this. The police investigation did not confirm the allegation. The license was restored on January 21, 2026.

stories.title: Government to release 81,000 police vacancies in UP:CM Yogi stresses timely recruitment, orders reshuffle of long-posted staff
stories.summary: More than 81,000 vacancies will be filled in the Uttar Pradesh Police. The announcement was made by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during a late-night review meeting of the police department on Thursday. The Chief Minister said that 2026–27 will be very important for youth preparing to join the Uttar Pradesh Police. Preparations are underway to recruit over 81,000 personnel within a year. He also directed officials to further strengthen law and order. He said police personnel posted for a long time in places like Raj Bhavan, the Chief Minister’s residence and police headquarters in Lucknow should be transferred. He asked officials to adopt a result-oriented approach and ensure accountability at every level. Recruitment will be conducted for these positions Officials informed the Chief Minister that recruitment will be conducted for more than 81,000 posts across various categories, including Sub-Inspectors, constables, radio assistant operators, computer operator Grade-A and confidential Sub-Inspectors. The recruitment process for some posts has already begun. The Chief Minister directed the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board to ensure that all direct recruitments are conducted transparently, fairly and in accordance with reservation rules, within a fixed timeline. He emphasised the use of technology to complete the process on time and strengthen trust among youth. stories.title: Bareilly professor breaks silence on ‘sexy’ remark row:Alleges attack by hired goons, says, 'Will continue writing on flaws in govt and system'
stories.summary: A controversy at Bareilly College has intensified after Professor Alok Kumar Khare, accused of making an objectionable social media remark about a BJP woman leader, alleged that he was attacked by “hired goons” and vowed to continue writing about systemic shortcomings. Speaking in an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Khare said, “ABVP used to be a good organisation, but now indisciplined elements are being recruited. Some hired miscreants even tried to attack me. I am not anti-government, but I will keep writing about flaws in the system.” What triggered the controversy The row began when Khare, then Chief Proctor of Bareilly College, shared a social media post commenting on BJP leader Komapella Madhavi Latha in a derogatory manner. The post quickly went viral, sparking outrage among student groups, especially members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). On April 1, ABVP workers stormed the principal’s office, raised slogans, and allegedly manhandled Khare. The situation escalated to the point where some female students reportedly attempted to assault him. Amid rising tensions, Principal Dr. Om Prakash Rai removed Khare from the post of Chief Proctor and dissolved the entire proctorial board. ‘This was a planned conspiracy’ Khare claimed the incident was premeditated, The social media post was just an excuse. A conspiracy was hatched with the help of some insiders on campus to target and humiliate me. I had already submitted my resignation three days earlier. He alleged that external elements were brought in, Students of this campus would never stoop to grabbing a teacher by the collar. These were outsiders. We are reviewing CCTV footage and will take legal action. Allegations against ABVP The professor criticized ABVP’s recent functioning, Earlier, ABVP had disciplined members. Now, unruly individuals have entered the organization. Many of those present during the incident were not even members. He further alleged that political backing emboldens such behavior, When those in power offer protection, taking legal action becomes difficult. This increases their confidence. Fear for life, demands action Khare expressed concern for his safety, If they can behave like this with the Chief Proctor, they can do anything. I’ve been warned not to move alone on campus. There is a real threat to my life. He said a formal complaint has been submitted and action is awaited, If no action is taken in two to three days, we will protest and approach higher authorities. Clarification on social media post Defending himself, Khare said, I am a science teacher and often write against superstition. I did not even know who the woman was. If someone had objected, they could have approached me. I would have apologized. Violence is not justified. ‘I am not anti-government’ Responding to allegations of being anti-government, Khare stated, I do not write against the government, but I do highlight flaws in the system. Law and order may have improved, but issues in education remain. He added that raising concerns—such as pollution or problems faced by farmers—should not be seen as opposition but as stating facts. A career marked by controversy Professor Khare has a teaching career spanning over 35 years. He completed his graduation in 1984 from YD College, Lakhimpur Kheri, and later earned a PhD in Botany. Before joining Bareilly College, he taught at Sacred Heart Degree College in Sitapur and is also an authorized research supervisor at Rohilkhand University. However, he has frequently been in the spotlight due to his outspoken social media posts.

stories.title: Construction, award of highway projects at 7-year low in 2025-26
stories.summary: Highway construction and new project awards in 2025-26 hit a seven-year low, with less than 10,000 km built and only 7,000 km awarded. This decline is attributed to stricter land availability pre-conditions and fewer state highways being converted to National Highways. Agencies are prioritizing economic corridors and expressways to avoid project delays and cost escalations.

stories.title: Justice B V Nagarathna: Women cannot be 'untouchables' for 3 days every month
stories.summary: Justice B.V. Nagarathna strongly criticized the historical practice of isolating menstruating women, deeming it a form of "untouchability." While hearing arguments on the Sabarimala temple entry ban, she questioned the validity of such social customs. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta countered, arguing the deity's unique attributes and devotees' faith should not be tested by gender equality standards.

stories.title: Empty cylinders drive migrants back home
stories.summary: Soaring LPG prices are forcing migrant workers back to Bihar. Families are disembarking at Patna Junction, their journeys driven by unaffordable cooking gas in cities. Construction workers and factory hands cite exorbitant costs, with some stating two days' wages barely cover a kilogram of LPG. This exodus highlights the severe economic strain impacting livelihoods.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's absence fuels alliance friction buzz
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has made multiple visits to Tamil Nadu for campaigning, while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's absence has fueled speculation about discord within the Congress-DMK alliance. stories.title: Amit Shah slams Mallikarjun Kharge for likening BJP-RSS to 'snake'

Shah asserted that such remarks are undemocratic and urged voters to decisively defeat the Congress in upcoming elections, stating the party has become a threat to the democratic system under Rahul Gandhi's leadership.

stories.title: Amid Iran war, government extends freeze on channel TRPs
stories.summary: Television rating points for news channels have been suspended for another four weeks by the information and broadcasting ministry. This decision, citing concerns over sensationalizing the West Asia conflict, aims to curb unwarranted sensationalism and speculative content. The move, following a previous suspension linked to alleged manipulation, signals increased regulatory oversight during crises.

Congress leaders decried the move as a 'witch hunt' and misuse of state power, demanding a probe into Sarma's wife's alleged foreign assets and passports.

stories.title: EC imposes ban on exit polls for assembly polls in five states till April 29
'Fake AI campaign': Himanta's all-out war on Congress leader Pawan Khera over passport and property allegations
Cabinet secretariat wants fire safety out of National Building Code, BIS panel recommends otherwise
stories.summary: A Bureau of Indian Standards technical committee urged the cabinet secretariat's deregulation cell to retain fire and life safety in the National Building Code, deeming it crucial for public safety. The cell had proposed moving these critical aspects to separate handbooks, a move experts argue could create death traps.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu elections: Leema Rose, 'lottery king’s' wife, richest in fray with Rs 1,000cr assets
SIR row: Mamata Banerjee claims names of people belonging to 'specific communities' deleted from voter rolls
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has accused authorities of selectively removing names from voter rolls ahead of assembly elections. She stated that nearly 91 lakh voters were deleted post-revision, with her intervention in the Supreme Court restoring about 32 lakh names. Banerjee alleged that specific communities were targeted in these deletions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia mandates 100% employment of KSA nationals in 69 private sector jobs
'Puppet': Stalin hits out at Puducherry CM
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin criticises Puducherry's chief minister N Rangasamy as a puppet. He claims the LG holds excessive power, sidelining the elected government. Stalin argues that this power imbalance hinders governance and accountability. He advocates for full statehood to restore authority to the elected leadership. The upcoming polls are framed as a vote against this imbalance.

stories.title: Cambodia honours its most famous landmine-sniffing rat, Magawa, with a statue
Artemis II astronauts observe Moon during flyby; NASA shares image
'Bleeding profusely, hiding in crevice': Trump discloses details of daring rescue of downed US pilot in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump detailed a daring US rescue of a downed F-15E officer in Iran, who survived nearly 48 hours behind enemy lines despite severe injuries. The complex mission involved 155 aircraft and intelligence tactics to confuse Iranian forces, culminating in a successful extraction despite last-minute complications.

stories.title: ‘God knows how many parts Pak will be divided this time’: Rajnath Singh hits out at Khawaja Asif over 'Kolkata threat', recalls 1971 split
stories.summary: India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has strongly criticized Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif for his provocative statement targeting Kolkata. Singh warned Islamabad against repeating past mistakes, referencing the 1971 division of Pakistan. This exchange follows Asif's threat to strike Kolkata if India launches a "false-flag operation."

stories.title: Indian woman on visit visa dies in UAE’s Sharjah, body repatriated after month-long delay over financial struggles
Assam passport row: Police search Pawan Khera’s Delhi residence after FIR by Himanta’s wife
stories.summary: Assam Police searched Congress leader Pawan Khera's Delhi residence following an FIR by Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's wife over passport allegations. Khera had claimed Sarma's wife held three passports, a charge denied by the BJP. The Chief Minister vowed strong action, accusing Congress of using unauthorized documents and alleging Pakistani links.

stories.title: Kerala elections: Venugopal writes to CM Vijayan, alleges 'deal' with BJP; questions 'breakfast meeting' with Sitharaman
16-year hunt ends as LeT operative among five held in Srinagar crackdown
'Much-awaited announcement': Ex-Punjab Congress leader Navjot Kaur Sidhu launches Bharatiya Rashtrawadi Party
'List stands frozen': Nearly 91 lakh voters deleted from Bengal rolls after SIR
stories.summary: Nearly 91 lakh names were removed from West Bengal's electoral rolls after a special revision exercise. The Election Commission's data shows significant deletions, impacting the voter base. While some deletions were finalized, others remain under adjudication. Electoral rolls for the first phase of assembly elections have now been frozen.

stories.title: No personal oral hearing needed before labelling bank accounts as fraud: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that banks are not required to provide personal oral hearings before classifying accounts as fraudulent. However, banks must furnish customers with a forensic audit report prior to such classification. This decision acknowledges the infeasibility of individual hearings given the significant rise in bank fraud cases.

stories.title: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri heads to Washington to review 'full spectrum' India–US ties
Artemis 2: NASA re-establishes contact with Artemis 2 after a 40-minute blackout
Saudi Arabia, Russia 90-day visa-free travel begins from May 11: Ministry announces
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Russia are implementing a visa-free travel agreement starting May 11, allowing citizens short-term visits of up to 90 days annually for tourism, business, and family. This initiative, stemming from a December 2025 deal, aims to foster closer people-to-people connections and enhance bilateral cooperation, though work, study, residency, and religious travel still require visas.

stories.title: Assam assembly polls: Campaigning to stop as EC enforces silence period from today
stories.summary: The Election Commission has announced the commencement of the silence period for Assam legislative assembly elections from 5:00 PM today, prohibiting all forms of campaigning, including public meetings and social media dissemination. This 48-hour period before polling on April 9 aims to ensure a free and fair electoral process, with strict compliance mandated for all stakeholders.

stories.title: Did US use F-15E rescue op as cover to seize uranium? Iran claims ‘deception mission’
stories.summary: Iran alleges a US rescue mission for a downed F-15E crew member may have been a cover to steal enriched uranium, a claim the US dismisses as a complex, intelligence-led extraction. The operation, described as daring, occurred deep inside Iranian territory amid escalating regional conflict.

stories.title: A tiny hole in Greenland reveals how creatures survived extreme climate 210 million years ago
'Hub for arming, financing regime’s proxies': Israel targets 3 Iran airports
Rajnath lays foundation stones for 3 new centres at R&R, new infra at Base Hospital
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated new medical facilities at Army Hospital (Research & Referral) and Base Hospital, Delhi Cantonment. These state-of-the-art centers will enhance tertiary care for the Armed Forces Medical Services, focusing on ophthalmology, oncology, and joint replacements. Singh emphasized the critical role of health security in national defense and military operations.

stories.title: Judiciary graft chapter: 3 academicians move Supreme Court against NCERT association ban
KMVN gas manager dies, colleagues cite 'work pressure'
EC seeks report on BJP pick's 'love jihad' remark
AIIMS-B teams up with Dutch experts to bring personalised meds to patients
Jaishankar to Iran counterpart: Back efforts to stop war
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar discussed West Asia's stability with his Iranian counterpart, emphasizing support for regional peace efforts. Conversations with Qatar and the UAE also touched upon military escalation and its security implications. Iran highlighted alleged "heinous crimes" by "aggressors," while Qatar urged an end to "unjustified Iranian attacks" and stressed de-escalation.

stories.title: Japanese tourist molested near Jaipur's Jaigarh Fort, FIR lodged but no arrests yet
stories.summary: Five youths are accused of sexually harassing a Japanese tourist near Jaigarh Fort in Jaipur. The group allegedly pushed the woman, held her, and attempted to kiss her before fleeing when she raised the alarm and a security guard approached. An FIR has been registered, but no arrests have been made.

stories.title: “Best friend’s grave”: Laura Loomer slams Candace Owens after she calls President administration satanic, drags Charlie Kirk into feud
stories.summary: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens are in a public fight after Owens called Donald Trump’s administration “satanic.” Loomer hit back with a personal comment that hinted at Charlie Kirk. The debate quickly moved beyond politics into personal accusations. Owens also spoke about Tucker Carlson and shared strong views about global events and future political possibilities involving Erika Kirk.

stories.title: Claims of 27L Bengal voters in doubtful list rejected, can't vote
stories.summary: Nearly 27 lakh voters in West Bengal face exclusion from the electoral roll as their claims were rejected by judicial officers. The Supreme Court has ruled against the inclusion of names pending appeals, citing the burden on tribunals and potential chaos. Deletions now stand at 88.8 lakh, impacting 11.6% of the electorate.

stories.title: Supreme Court to CBI: Probe ' 1,200cr contracts to Arunachal CM's kin'
Indian couple jailed in UK for running companies despite legal ban; involved in £2 million tax fraud
Wards to flowers: Tulip Garden trip for young cancer fighters
stories.summary: Cancer-stricken children experienced a mood transformation during a visit to Srinagar's Tulip Garden, part of SKIMS' novel immunotherapy initiative. The outing aimed to boost their immunity and optimism, offering a much-needed respite from hospital wards and providing reassurance to both the children and their families.

stories.title: Rapper 6ix9ine officially retires from music, shifts focus to streaming
stories.summary: Rapper 6ix9ine, also known as Daniel Hernandez, has announced his retirement from the music industry, declaring it "washed up." He revealed this decision during a livestream with Adin Ross, stating his intention to focus entirely on streaming. This unexpected move has garnered mixed reactions from fans, with some supporting his new venture and others expressing disappointment.

stories.title: Indian‑origin student dies after drowning in New Zealand lake; parents seek urgent repatriation
Jammu & Kashmir has lost 315 lakes since 1967
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir has lost nearly 3,000 hectares of lakes since 1967, with 315 lakes disappearing and remaining ones shrinking. This significant loss, detailed in a CAG report, degraded ecosystems and contributed to the devastating 2014 Kashmir floods by reducing natural flood buffers.

stories.title: Landslides block Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in Ramban
stories.summary: Heavy rains unleashed massive landslides in Ramban, completely obstructing the vital Jammu-Srinagar National Highway. Mud and falling stones choked the road between Karol Bridge and Chanderkote, stranding numerous vehicles. Officials indicated that clearing efforts are underway, but continuous rainfall significantly hinders any immediate reopening of this crucial all-weather route.

stories.title: Jammu man lured into Russian job and sent to war zone killed
stories.summary: A 23-year-old Jammu man, Sachin Khajuria, who went to Russia for a job, was sent to the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war and has now been cremated after his death was confirmed. He is the second from Jammu to die in the conflict, with families alleging youths were duped by agents promising civilian jobs but were forced into the army.

stories.title: Not end of road for those who didn't get selected in H-1B lottery: Immigration attorney explains 8 best options
This 2000-year-old coin collected as bus fare in the 1950s, turns out to be a rare artefact
All the Rakai drama from MrBeast’s $1,000,000 streamer event you need to know
stories.summary: MrBeast's million-dollar streamer challenge saw YourRAGE claim the top prize. However, contestant Rakai's on-stage outburst after elimination and subsequent online dispute with El Rubius fans created significant drama. Security was called to remove Rakai. This controversy, alongside the competition, made the event highly memorable for viewers. The incident highlighted the intense pressure faced by participants.

stories.title: Indian-origin Subu Vedam avoids deportation, judge says he 'has grown as a person'

Chhattisgarh CM to meet PM Modi, Amit Shah; roadmap for post-Maoist growth in focus
Greg Abbott trolled for old Diwali video when he said 'Texas will be a land for the Indian community'
‘God was watching us’: Donald Trump hails Iran pilot rescue op, warns media over leak - top quotes
stories.summary: As a 48-hour deadline for Iran approaches, President Trump warned the nation could be "taken out in one night." He detailed a complex rescue operation for two downed airmen, involving over 170 US military aircraft and facing close-range gunfire. Trump also vowed to identify a source who leaked details of the operation, citing national security concerns.

stories.title: Steve Bannon contempt of Congress case: How conviction over J6 now faces possible dismissal
CEC impeachment motion rejected: What can opposition do next?
No dude left behind: Trump toots US success while warning Iran 'surrender or else…'
stories.summary: US President Trump issued a stark warning to Iran, threatening further destruction if they don't capitulate by his deadline. Amidst growing domestic unease about a potential quagmire, the US conducted a complex rescue mission for a downed airman, involving advanced technology and significant financial costs. Iran's claims of capturing personnel were disputed by US officials.

stories.title: ‘A proud moment’: PM Modi hails India’s ‘defining step’ in civil nuclear journey as Kalpakkam fast breeder reactor attains criticality
stories.summary: India has achieved a significant milestone in its nuclear energy program as the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam successfully attained criticality. Prime Minister Modi hailed this as a defining step, showcasing the nation's scientific prowess and engineering capabilities.

stories.title: Actor Matthew Marsden says he received threats for speaking about H-1B visa scam by Indians in Texas: 'If Brits were committing...'
Gigi Hadid breaks silence on being mentioned in Epstein files: 'I grew up privileged...'
Defiance or sabotage? What AAP's move in Kerala signals for Congress in assembly polls
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party's decision to contest all seats in Kerala assembly polls creates a new challenge for Congress. This move mirrors AAP's impact in Gujarat, where it reduced Congress's vote share. AAP's presence could alter the political landscape, potentially benefiting the ruling Left. The INDIA bloc faces internal friction as AAP expands its national footprint.

stories.title: Lindsey Graham says US is so close to strategic victory: 'Either via diplomacy or military action'
Florida man crashes electric bike into tricycle, found with three marijuana cigarettes

Lok Sabha Speaker, Rajya Sabha chairman reject impeachment motion against poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: The 10-page-long notice carried a chargesheet on seven counts. ​​The charges ranged from partisan conduct of CEC to mass disenfranchisement of voters. The opposition had also raised the issue of the way CEC handled SIR in previous elections like Bihar and forthcoming elections in states like West Bengal; his "proved misbehaviour"; his partial conduct towards a political party are also issues that find a mention in the notice.

stories.title: Soldier arrives at Louisiana base for training, ICE arrests his Honduran wife who was brought to US as toddler
Delhi Assembly security scare: Masked men placed bouquet inside Speaker's car - what we know so far
stories.summary: Three suspects were detained after a car breached Delhi Assembly security, placing a bouquet and garland in the Speaker's vehicle before fleeing. The SUV, with a UP registration, broke through Gate 2, triggering a high alert. Authorities conducted a thorough sweep, finding no explosives. The motive remains unclear amid recent bomb threats.

stories.title: 'Will continue war ...': Iran rejects temporary truce; sets condition for talks
stories.summary: Iran has finalised its demands for ending the conflict with the US and Israel, rejecting a temporary truce. Tehran conveyed its requirements through intermediaries, deeming earlier US proposals "excessive and illogical." Iran insists on a permanent end to hostilities, not a pause that allows adversaries to regroup.

stories.title: N Korea calls South Korean Prez Lee’s regret over drone incursions ‘wise’
stories.summary: North Korea has responded positively to South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's apology for drone incursions, calling it "fortunate and wise." Lee admitted government officials were involved, violating policy. This rare conciliatory tone follows years of hostility, though broader tensions persist between the two nations.

stories.title: Moldy food found in Indian restaurant in Texas, was forced to shut down
JK Rowling and the Tiresome Hollywood Activist
Punjab Police foil terror plot, arrest three linked to ISI-backed module
stories.summary: Punjab Police have dismantled an ISI-backed terror module planning grenade attacks on police establishments across multiple states. Three individuals were apprehended with two hand grenades and a pistol, bearing markings from Pakistan Ordnance Factory. Investigations revealed the operatives were in contact with Pakistan Intelligence Operatives via social media, acting on ISI handlers' directives.

Supreme Court asks Bengal's top bureaucrat to apologise over siege of SIR officers in Malda
stories.summary: Taking strong exception to the attack on judicial officers adjudicating objections to voter list exclusions in West Bengal’s Malda district, the Supreme Court on Thursday said there was a breakdown of law and order in the state and issued show-cause notices to the chief secretary, DGP, district magistrate and SP, asking why action should not be taken against them.

stories.title: UAPA terror case: US citizen, 6 Ukrainians sent to 30-day judicial custody
stories.summary: Seven foreign nationals, including six Ukrainians and one US citizen, were remanded to 30 days' judicial custody in Delhi for alleged terror links. The NIA claims they supplied weapons and training to Indian insurgent groups, with connections to Myanmar's ethnic armed factions. Investigations are ongoing into their motives and activities.

stories.title: 'Laughable questions': Assam CM Himanta Sarma’s wife slams Gaurav Gogoi over passport row; questions his wife
stories.summary: Assam CM's wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sharma, vehemently denied Congress claims of holding foreign passports and undisclosed overseas assets. She challenged Assam Congress leader Gaurav Gogoi to disclose his wife's bank account details in Pakistan. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused the Congress of using fake, Pakistan-sourced documents and stated an FIR was filed.

stories.title: Australians react as 33,000 Sydney residents and 8,600 Melbourne natives flee due to rising immigrant population
UAE extends Nafis programme to 2040; 176,000 Emiratis employed so far
stories.summary: The UAE's Nafis programme is now extended until 2040, a significant move to boost Emirati employment in the private sector. New initiatives offer support for children and wives of Emiratis working in private companies, alongside expanded children's allowances. This long-term strategy aims to build a sustainable national workforce and reduce reliance on public sector jobs.

Who is Dr Ashok Jain? Indian-origin paediatrician, who built a $750,000 school in his Rajasthan village
Delhi Assembly security scare: Suspect caught on cam; 3 detained, car seized
stories.summary: A Tata Sierra car with UP registration breached the Delhi Assembly's Gate No. 2 on Monday, with an occupant placing a bouquet before driving off. Delhi Police have arrested the accused and seized the vehicle. Security was in place at the VIP gate, and no suspicious objects were found.

Ukraine launched 7,347 drones at Russia in March, outpaces Moscow for first time since 2022
stories.summary: Ukraine has outpaced Russia in drone attacks for the first time since the war began. Kyiv's forces targeted Russian oil infrastructure, aiming to disrupt funding for the conflict. Russia reported intercepting a record number of Ukrainian drones. Both nations continue to rely heavily on long-range strikes, raising concerns about the war's potential to spread.

stories.title: NASA's Artemis II mission: Crew honours Jeremy Hansen with ‘astronaut gold pin’, an elite spaceflight award
Excise policy scam case: 'I will argue myself', Kejriwal tells Delhi HC in recusal plea; next hearing on April 13
stories.summary: Delhi High Court heard the CBI's challenge to Arvind Kejriwal's discharge in the excise policy case. Kejriwal, present with his wife, declared his intent to argue his recusal application personally, asserting his legal rights. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta objected, citing procedural rules. The court issued notice on Kejriwal's recusal plea.

stories.title: Where are the astronauts living inside the Orion spacecraft on their mission to the Moon
'You should resign': Mamata hits out at PM Modi's silence on Pakistan's threat to strike Kolkata
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on Pakistan's threat to strike Kolkata. She criticized the PM for targeting Bengal during rallies but not addressing the specific threat, demanding his resignation. Banerjee asserted that threats to the state would not be tolerated.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Max Planck: “Science cannot solve the ultimate mystery of nature. And that is because, in the last analysis, we ourselves are a part of the mystery that we are trying to solve.”
From job creation to free bus travel for women: What Congress is offering in Puducherry manifesto
stories.summary: Congress is campaigning for Puducherry assembly elections with a strong focus on jobs and social security. The party promises Rs 2,000 monthly for unemployed youth and 30,000 new jobs. Free bus travel for women and Rs 20 lakh health insurance are also pledged. Full statehood for Puducherry remains a key promise.

stories.title: 'Never outshine the master': Raghav Chadha's cryptic Instagram post amid rift with AAP leadership
Fire chiefs killed in crash: Walnuttown leaders die in Route 222 collision; pair arrested after fleeing
Germany is building a 364-metre world’s tallest wind turbine in a coal mine, and it could transform renewable power
Chile's Kast to visit Argentina for first foreign tripx
stories.summary: Chile's far-right President Jose Antonio Kast is scheduled to meet with his Argentine counterpart in Buenos Aires on Monday, marking his first trip abroad since taking office in March. The visit continues the tradition of Chilean presidents making Argentina their first official state trip.

stories.title: Puducherry polls: Rahul Gandhi promises full statehood for UT if Congress wins
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi pledged full statehood for Puducherry if Congress forms the government, accusing the current administration of being remotely controlled by Delhi. He also outlined promises including monthly support for unemployed youth, job creation, free bus travel for women, relaxed government job age limits, and Rs 20 lakh healthcare insurance for every family.

stories.title: TVK chief Vijay calls off Chennai campaign
'Serious lapse in duty': ADM served show-cause notice over Malda judicial officers 'hostage' episode
Why Artemis II astronauts lost contact with Earth for 40 minutes during its Moon mission

SC orders CBI inquiry into allegations that Arunachal PWD contracts were awarded to firms linked to CM Pema Khandu’s kin
Filipino bakery owner in UAE offers free grocery to expats facing job loss and unpaid leave: Each branch to distribute 100 packets
stories.summary: A UAE-based pastry chain owner, Maria Paz Banaag-Marquez, is distributing 300 free grocery packets to expatriate families facing financial hardship due to reduced wages and unpaid leave. Each Dh75 packet contains essential staples. Maria, who moved to the UAE in 2008, is personally funding additional aid, demonstrating her gratitude to the nation.

stories.title: UAE residents to get six-day public holiday in 2026 for Arafah Day and Eid Al Adha: How to extend it further
'Muslim-sounding' radio message from missing F-15 airman sparked Iran trap fears, nearly jeopardised rescue
BJP Foundation Day: PM Modi hails workers’ selfless service, reiterates ‘Viksit Bharat’ vision
Sweden releases tanker after oil-spill probe
stories.summary: Swedish authorities have released a tanker they had suspected of causing an oil spill after finding no offence could be proved. But the coast guard said late on Saturday that Cameroon had confirmed the vessel's registration and no environmental offence could be proved, "There are therefore no further grounds for continuing the investigation."

stories.title: 'False and fabricated': Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma alleges ‘Pakistani link’ after Congress claims on wife’s passports
stories.summary: The political climate in Assam has heated up as Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused Congress leaders Pawan Khera and Gaurav Gogoi of presenting forged travel documents sourced from a Pakistani broadcaster during a recent press conference. Together with his wife, Sarma has filed a formal complaint, arguing that the passports were doctored.

stories.title: Donald Trump asks Tehran to open Strait of Hormuz; Iran says 'lost the keys': Where things stand after a month of war
Texas man pleads guilty to $37 million US Air Force fraud, channelled bribes to 'Godfather' and 'Al Capone'
'Denying no property in Dubai?': Pawan Khera escalates attack on Himanta, wife over foreign assets
stories.summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera has accused Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma and his wife of holding multiple foreign passports and having undisclosed overseas properties and shell companies. Sarma has vehemently denied these allegations, labeling them as politically motivated lies and announcing defamation lawsuits against Khera, vowing to hold him accountable.

stories.title: 'Dragging US towards living hell': Iran slams Trump's 'Tuesday threat' over Strait of Hormuz closure
stories.summary: Iran has strongly responded to US President Donald Trump's recent threat concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran's Parliament Speaker accused Trump of reckless escalation driven by Israeli interests. Trump had issued an ultimatum demanding the reopening of the vital oil route. Iran rejected the threat, with military officials calling Trump's remarks 'stupid'.

stories.title: Congress accuses govt of 'bulldozing' its delimitation proposal which is nothing but a 'weapon of mass distraction'
stories.summary: The Congress has strongly criticized the Modi government's delimitation proposal, alleging it unfairly benefits larger, populous states and diminishes the political influence of southern and northeastern regions. Leaders claim the plan to increase Lok Sabha seats will widen existing disparities, calling it a "Weapon of Mass Distraction" amidst national crises.

stories.title: What is the “Kennedy curse”: A closer look at the family’s history
"This is a satanic administration": Candace Owens sparks online storm with latest comments targeting the White House
stories.summary: Candace Owens is facing widespread backlash after controversial remarks sparked intense debate online. A viral response criticizing her influence and rhetoric has further fueled the discussion. Her statements have divided opinion, with some supporting her stance while others see it as extreme. The controversy highlights growing tensions and shifting dynamics within political commentary on social media platforms.

stories.title: Beef row: Chief minister vows action against AJP nominee's kin
stories.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma has brought beef consumption into his election campaign, targeting Congress ally AJP's candidate Kunki Chowdhury. He accused her parents of eating beef and vowed action under the Cattle Prevention Act post-election. Sarma challenged Chowdhury to disown her parents' actions, emphasizing the religious sentiments of 'Sanatani' people and the sanctity of religious sites.

stories.title: RG Kar victim's mom threatens to 'thrash' Didi, TMC seeks action
500 judges on SIR duty, cases pile up across Bengal courts
EC seizes voter inducements worth over 650cr from poll-bound states, UT
stories.summary: Election Commission teams have seized over Rs 650 crore in potential voter inducements across five poll-bound states, with West Bengal leading seizures at Rs 319 crore. Freebies, drugs, and cash formed the bulk of the confiscated items. This figure is on track to surpass last year's record of Rs 1,000 crore in seizures.

stories.title: Odisha bans sale of LPG cylinders in open market
stories.summary: Odisha has banned the open sale of LPG cylinders to combat black marketing. Only customers who have completed e-KYC can now purchase them from authorized dealers. The government assures sufficient supply, with delivery timelines of 25 days for urban and 45 days for rural consumers. This move follows recent seizures of cylinders for illegal resale.

stories.summary: Homes Fully Served, Biz Demand 80%

stories.title: IMD predicts cooler temps in north-west India, rain likely
stories.summary: North-west India will experience two western disturbances this week. Peak activity is expected on April 7-8. This will bring below normal to near normal day temperatures and a wet spell to the region. Other parts of the country will also see wet spells with thunderstorms and lightning until April 9.

stories.title: Malda siege of judicial officers proof of jungle raj, says Modi in Bengal
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi criticized Bengal's law and order, citing the confinement of judicial officers in Malda as evidence of "jungle raj." He linked electoral roll revision to identifying "illegal settlers" and accused the TMC of protecting infiltrators, while also questioning their manifesto's name and warning of accountability after the elections.

stories.title: Mumbai seafarer's remains brought home, family seeks DNA proof
No Brahmin fielded by major parties in TN
stories.summary: For the first time in 35 years, AIADMK has not fielded any Brahmin candidates in Tamil Nadu polls, reflecting the community's waning influence. Major parties like DMK, Congress, and BJP also lack Brahmin nominees, while TVK and NTK have fielded candidates, targeting constituencies with significant Brahmin votes.

stories.title: SNL UK faces backlash over crude joke referencing Mark Zuckerberg and Adolf Hitler
Indian-origin doctor to pay $14 million to settle allegations against him in US; performed unnecessary procedures
HC lets married teen live with man of her choice
stories.summary: A 19-year-old married woman in Bhopal has been granted legal permission to live independently with a man of her choice. She testified to the Madhya Pradesh High Court that her much older husband mistreated her and she did not wish to return to her parents. The court placed her under the Shourya Didi framework for six months.

stories.title: SpaceX's Starship could cut travel time to Uranus in half
Women's rights & religion: CJI-led 9-J bench includes all faiths, and a woman
stories.summary: A nine-judge Supreme Court bench, comprising judges from diverse faiths and a woman, will hear crucial cases on women's rights versus religious practices starting April 7. This bench aims to settle long-standing disputes, including women's entry into temples, mosques, and Parsi fire temples, and the practice of FGM. The court's 2018 Sabarimala judgment sparked these broader legal challenges.

stories.title: Punjab ‘my soul’, says Chadha in response to AAP Punjab unit charges
stories.summary: Estranged AAP MP Raghav Chadha strongly refuted allegations from the party's Punjab unit that he failed to raise state issues in Parliament. He asserted his commitment to Punjab, highlighting numerous issues he has addressed, including pending funds, agricultural distress, and the drug menace. Chadha dismissed the claims as baseless and motivated, vowing that truth and facts would prevail.

stories.title: Petition filed in SC challenging amended 'transgender persons' law
stories.summary: Transgender rights activists have filed a Supreme Court petition challenging the constitutional validity of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026. The amendments remove self-perceived identity as the basis for TG certificates and introduce a medical board, moving away from the NALSA judgment's affirmation of personal dignity and choice.

stories.title: ISRO launches Mission MITRA in Ladakh for astronaut study: Inside the 3,500m experiment testing human survival in space-like conditions
Who is Sarinasadat Hosseiny? Grandniece of Iranian general Qasem Soleimani arrested by ICE
Porcupines push saffron to brink in Kashmir
stories.summary: Kashmir's prized saffron is under siege from an unexpected foe: the Indian crested porcupine. These nocturnal rodents are burrowing underground, destroying saffron corms and decimating harvests. Production has plummeted, threatening the livelihoods and identity tied to Pampore's "red gold." stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin has strongly criticized the CBSE's new curriculum framework. He labels it a linguistic imposition that favors Hindi over regional languages. Stalin argues this policy undermines federalism and marginalizes non-Hindi-speaking states. He urges the Union government to respect India's linguistic diversity and protect students' rights across all states

stories.title: ‘I thought it was spam’: Indian expat wins Dh20 million in Abu Dhabi Big Ticket draw
stories.summary: An Indian expatriate in Oman, Shanthanu Shettigar, has won the Dh20 million grand prize in Abu Dhabi's Big Ticket draw. He purchased the winning ticket with a friend, and the duo will share the life-changing jackpot. The draw also awarded five other winners with Dh1 million each.

stories.title: Iran downs F-15, A-10 jets: First US combat aircraft losses in over 20 years
stories.summary: Iran has shot down two US military aircraft, an F-15E Strike Eagle and an A-10 attack aircraft, marking the first such incidents in over two decades. Despite US claims of Iran's weakened capabilities, these events highlight Tehran's continued ability to retaliate, possibly with shoulder-fired missiles, even as US forces conduct extensive operations.

stories.title: How to survive in enemy territory after jet goes down—High-risk journey of a shot-down pilot
Debris from aerial interception strikes building in Dubai's Marina
stories.summary: Debris from an aerial interception struck a building in Dubai Marina, authorities confirmed Saturday. No fire or injuries were reported following the incident, which occurred amid ongoing regional conflict. This follows earlier attacks in the UAE, including one at a gas facility and a fire on a Kuwaiti oil tanker.

stories.title: CM Rekha Gupta unveils Delhi's air pollution mitigation plan for 2026
Petrol shock, free rides & more: How is Pakistan dealing with Hormuz energy crisis
stories.summary: Pakistan grapples with soaring fuel prices, prompting free public transport in Islamabad and Punjab for 30 days. Despite a revised petrol price, public anger persists. The government aims to ease economic burdens amid global energy disruptions and IMF pressure, with similar measures seen in Karachi and Bangladesh.

stories.title: Those hit by 'kissing disease' are 3 times more likely to develop multiple sclerosis
Shashi Tharoor's convoy blocked in Kerala's Wandoor, five men assault his gunman, driver
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor's convoy faced an alleged attack in Kerala's Wandoor on Friday evening. Two vehicles reportedly blocked the road, leading to an assault on Tharoor's gunman and driver when they attempted to clear the obstruction. Police have arrested one of the five identified accused and are pursuing the others.

stories.title: 'One by one': Another US jet after F-15E crashes into Hormuz after being shot down by Iran; watch
stories.summary: An American A-10 Thunderbolt II jet crashed into the Strait of Hormuz shortly after an F-15E Strike Eagle was reportedly shot down over Iran. The Iranian embassy in South Africa shared footage, claiming "American fighter jets are being shot down one by one." The A-10's pilot was safely rescued, though details surrounding the crash remain scarce.

'Anxiety among minorities': Shashi Tharoor questions FCRA Ammendment Bill
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor expressed skepticism regarding reports of the Centre withdrawing the FCRA Amendment Bill, warning of its potential reintroduction. He stated the opposition will remain vigilant to prevent amendments causing anxiety among religious minorities. Opposition MPs had previously protested the bill, citing concerns for NGOs and minority groups

stories.title: Sharma diverges from Congress line on West Asia, hails government’s diplomacy
Middle East continues to boil: Iran rejects US 48-hour ceasefire proposal
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly rejected a US proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire, with an unnamed source citing the offer was delivered via an intermediary. Tehran insists on a guaranteed, permanent end to hostilities and has dismissed claims by US President Trump about seeking a temporary truce.

stories.title: Delhi, Baku work to fix ties after Pakistan row
7th India-flagged LPG tanker crosses Hormuz, 17 in queue
stories.summary: In a significant maritime achievement, an Indian LPG tanker has successfully maneuvered through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, flanked by six compatriots that have already reached Indian shores. However, the tension persists as seventeen Indian vessels, two of which are LPG carriers, hold position on the western side, biding their time for a chance to make the journey.

stories.title: Special session a violation of election code, claims Congress
stories.summary: The Congress party has criticized the BJP's recently announced 'special session', accusing it of violating campaign regulations, particularly regarding the contentious women's quota bill, which they claim is aimed at influencing voters in Tamil Nadu and Bengal. They express concern over proposed adjustments to parliamentary seats, warning it could marginalize smaller states and exacerbate regional inequalities.

stories.title: Government confident of cross-party support for women’s quota bills
stories.summary: The government plans to reconvene Parliament for a special session to pass women's reservation legislation for 2029. Despite opposition parties questioning the timing and motives, they've largely supported the proposal itself. The NDA is confident due to broad past support and women's growing influence as voters, anticipating passage of key bills.

stories.title: ‘Game changer’: England town stopped mowing 8 miles of grass and nature came back instantly while saving £25,000 a year
stories.summary: Rotherham town stopped mowing roadside grass and planted wildflowers. This policy change saved the town £25,000 annually. Wildlife returned in noticeable numbers. The verges transformed into colourful corridors of life. This initiative is now a model for cities seeking cost savings and biodiversity support. It shows how simple changes can yield significant environmental benefits.

stories.title: India’s third home-grown N-sub commissioned; Rajnath also launches stealth frigate, large cavitation tunnel facility at Vizag
stories.summary: India's naval strength significantly bolstered with the commissioning of INS Aridhaman, its third indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, enhancing its second-strike capability. The vessel boasts advanced stealth and increased missile capacity. Additionally, the stealth frigate INS Taragiri was inducted, alongside the foundation stone laid for a crucial naval research facility, underscoring India's growing maritime prowess and self-reliance.

stories.title: HAL imposes ‘contractual penalties’ on GE for Tejas engine delivery delay; PSU chief says Russia made presentation on Su-57 jet
stories.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited anticipates receiving 20 F404 engines from General Electric by December, with a sixth for the Tejas Mark 1A expected by April-end. HAL is imposing contractual penalties on GE for engine supply delays. Meanwhile, all 34 Tejas jets are set to resume flying from April 8 after software issues were resolved, following a recent grounding incident.

stories.summary: Ryan Pownall is a Canadian entrepreneur and podcast host who recently made headlines after TMZ reported an alleged argument with Alissa Violet that led to her arrest. The couple dated for nine months and have now split. Violet, known for past relationships with Jake Paul and FaZe Banks, has not responded to the report so far.

stories.title: Won’t be cowed, says Raghav, AAP brass says he indulged in ‘soft PR’
stories.summary: After Raghav Chadha's ousting as deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha, AAP leaders launched an intense critique, branding him as overly focused on superficial publicity while neglecting critical party ideologies. His peers challenged his muted stance on urgent political affairs and his conspicuous lack of presence at protests, suggesting a possible intimidation by PM Modi.

stories.title: “Those flirty texts”: Perez Hilton reacts as Prince Harry resurfaced chats with journalist raise concerns for Meghan Markle
stories.summary: Prince Harry’s old flirty messages with journalist Charlotte Griffiths have come out during his court case against Associated Newspapers. The chats, from 2011–2012, have sparked reactions, including from Perez Hilton. Reports say Meghan Markle is upset as the messages go public. Prince Harry has said he ended contact after learning Griffiths was a journalist. The court decision is still pending.

stories.title: Government moves to end toll waiver on ID display; no cash at booths from April 10
stories.summary: Toll payments will go cashless from April 10, with no cash transactions accepted. Vehicles without FASTags can pay via UPI at 1.25 times the normal fee, or face penalties. Exempted individuals must now use special FASTags or annual passes to prevent misuse and reduce arguments at toll plazas, paving the way for signal-free tolling.

stories.title: Supreme Court judge recuses self from case after reserving verdict
stories.summary: In a surprising twist, Justice K.V. Viswanathan of the Supreme Court opted to recuse himself from a case that had reached the judgment reservation stage. Upon reflection, he realized his prior role in representing the petitioner, Alchemist Asset Reconstruction Company, throughout his distinguished legal career.

stories.title: Government hopes to clear 5 crore pending cases with Jan Vishwas Bill
stories.summary: Government departments and prosecutors are urged to withdraw cases involving minor offences following the Jan Vishwas Bill's passage. This initiative aims to resolve millions of pending court cases by replacing jail terms with penalties for procedural lapses, particularly in healthcare. Serious offences remain under strict legal purview, offering relief for past minor violations.

stories.title: Supreme Court upholds harsher punishment for higher authority
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that higher rank officials face harsher penalties for service misdeeds due to increased responsibility. Upholding differential punishments for bank employees involved in misappropriating funds, the apex court reinstated a senior manager's sacking, while an officer faced forced retirement and a gunman a salary cut. Courts must exercise restraint in interfering with disciplinary actions.

stories.title: MeT forecasts heavy rains in Kashmir plains, snowfall in higher reaches
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir braces for a spell of heavy rain, gusty winds, and high-altitude snowfall over the next 36 hours. Srinagar experienced significant road flooding on Friday, prompting authorities to issue advisories for residents and tourists to avoid non-essential travel and exercise caution near water bodies. Erratic weather conditions are expected to persist until April 10.
